questions.explanation: By default the specifier coordinates products and materials, serving as the final check on whether they are compatible with one another.

questions.question: Which Division 01 section lists all of a project's proposed alternates and defines base-bid versus alternate scope?

options.A: Section 01 27 00 — Unit Prices, scheduling measured pricing, not each alternate
options.B: Section 01 26 00 — Contract Modification Procedures for changes and alternates
options.C: Section 01 21 00 — Allowances, carrying cash and quantity allowance scope
options.D: Section 01 23 00 — Alternates, listing each alternate and its scope

questions.explanation: Section 01 23 00 — Alternates is where all of the project's alternates are catalogued and where the distinction between base-bid work and alternate work is drawn. The other Division 01 sections handle unit prices, modifications, and allowances instead.

questions.question: When a product representative assists the design team with a specific product, the product is often included in the specifications as a:

options.A: Basis-of-design product
options.B: Performance-only product
options.C: Proprietary substitution
options.D: Sole-source product

questions.explanation: When a manufacturer's representative helps the team design around a particular product, that product is commonly named as the basis of design. Division 01 then sets out how comparable products from other makers can be accepted.

questions.question: Who has the responsibility to enforce consistent terminology and abbreviations across the construction documents?

options.A: The contractor
options.B: The owner
options.C: The A/E
options.D: Each consultant independently

questions.explanation: Keeping terms and abbreviations uniform across all of the documents falls to the A/E, who is positioned to enforce consistency across the disciplines.

questions.question: Why should consultants resist placing administrative general notes on their drawings?

options.A: Owners contractually prohibit placing any general notes on consultant-prepared drawings
options.B: Consultants lack the license to draft the Division 00 contract terms such notes contain
options.C: Drawings carry no contractual weight, so general notes on them are legally unenforceable
options.D: Such terms belong in Division 01, and duplicating them invites conflicting requirements

questions.explanation: Administrative requirements have their proper home in Division 01. Restating them as general notes on drawings creates a second copy that can drift out of sync with the original, producing conflicting requirements.

questions.question: Drafts of interim specification sections and consultant drawings are typically collected for coordination at which stages?

options.A: The 50 percent and 90 percent construction-document completion stages
options.B: At the single 100 percent construction-document submission, one of the stages
options.C: At bid opening and contract award, well after the 2 review milestones
options.D: During the punch list and project closeout near final completion

questions.explanation: Preliminary coordination of the documents is usually done at two checkpoints during their development, commonly the 50 percent and 90 percent completion milestones, so problems surface while there is still time to fix them.

questions.question: If a conflict arises between drawings and specifications, the conditions of the contract should state that:

options.A: The A/E makes a documented interpretation
options.B: Drawings always govern
options.C: The contractor selects the less costly option
options.D: Specifications always govern

questions.explanation: Drawings and specifications are meant to work together, so rather than ranking one above the other the conditions should direct that the A/E resolve any conflict through a written interpretation.

questions.question: Which CSI principle for locating information in the contract documents helps prevent overlap and duplication?

options.A: "Say it once and in the right place" to avoid duplication
options.B: "Coordinate the documents after bidding, accepting some duplication"
options.C: "Specify performance only and omit prescriptive detail"
options.D: "Where they overlap, the drawings govern the specifications"

questions.explanation: Stating each requirement a single time in its correct location keeps duplicate copies from appearing in the documents, which in turn removes the chance for those copies to disagree with each other.

questions.question: On a fast-track project issued in multiple bid packages, a modification made in an early package must be:

options.A: Resubmitted to the owner only for informational approval, not as a document change
options.B: Carried forward and incorporated into every later package issued for the project
options.C: Held back and disclosed only when the final bid package is issued for construction
options.D: Cancelled and the affected package reissued in full from the original master file

questions.explanation: When work is released in several packages, changes do not stay isolated. A modification made in an early package has to be carried into the later packages, and any change introduced later must be reconciled back into the earlier ones so all packages stay consistent.

questions.question: Particular attention during document coordination should be given to coordinating Division 01 with:

options.A: The geotechnical report bound in the available project information
options.B: The drawing sheet index and the project manual table of contents
options.C: The conditions of the contract governing the parties' obligations
options.D: The Division 09 finishes sections and their material schedules

questions.explanation: Division 01 and the conditions of the contract address overlapping administrative ground, so they need to be checked closely against one another to avoid gaps or contradictions between them.

questions.question: When consultants prepare their own specification sections, the prime A/E should:

options.A: Have the owner approve each consultant's sections independently
options.B: Defer Division 01 coordination to each consultant
options.C: Allow each consultant to set their own format
options.D: Assume responsibility for overall specification coordination

questions.explanation: Even when consultants write their own sections, overall coordination of the specifications remains the prime A/E's job, ensuring the separately authored sections fit together as one consistent project manual.

questions.question: What is the most effective protocol for relaying product information to the specifier?

options.A: Sharing the product information only at the scheduled design-milestone coordination meetings
options.B: Allowing any design-team member to email product information to the specifier directly
options.C: Requiring the specifier to pull product information from each consultant independently
options.D: Routing product information through a designated individual such as the PM or project A/E

questions.explanation: Funneling product information to the specifier through one designated point of contact, such as the project manager or project A/E, keeps the input organized and consistent instead of arriving piecemeal from many sources.

questions.question: Statements of precedence between contract documents are generally discouraged because they are:

options.A: Complementary
options.B: Owner-controlled
options.C: Subject to local code
options.D: Legally unenforceable

questions.explanation: Ranking one document above another is discouraged because the contract documents are intended to complement one another, with each supplying part of the complete requirements rather than competing for priority.

questions.question: Which delivery method most clearly brings the contractor into the project manual coordinating group during design?

options.A: Single-prime stipulated-sum, a delivery method selecting the contractor after design
options.B: Construction manager as advisor (CMa) engaged for preconstruction advice
options.C: Construction manager at risk (CMAR) or integrated project delivery (IPD)
options.D: Design-bid-build, the traditional sequence with the contractor bidding later

questions.explanation: CMAR and IPD engage the contractor while the design is still being developed. Because the contractor is contributing during design, it belongs in the group coordinating the project manual.

questions.question: Owners are typically responsible for providing which of the following project documents?

options.A: The geotechnical investigation report
options.B: Shop drawings and product data
options.C: Contractor's structural erection plans
options.D: Door hardware schedules and keying

questions.explanation: Furnishing the geotechnical report is normally the owner's responsibility, and it is included with or referenced in Division 00 as available project information for bidders to review.

questions.question: Product representatives can support design teams in all of these ways except:

options.A: Identifying comparable competitor products for equitable sections
options.B: Approving contractor substitution requests on the owner's behalf
options.C: Proposing alternative technology to achieve project cost savings
options.D: Reviewing draft specification sections for component completeness

questions.explanation: Product representatives can suggest cost-saving alternatives, review draft sections for completeness, and point out comparable competing products. What they cannot do is approve contractor substitution requests, which is not theirs to grant on the owner's behalf.

questions.question: Under AIA A201 and ConsensusDocs 200, a cash allowance is typically limited to:

options.A: All of the contractor's labor, taxes, overhead, and profit for the allowance item
options.B: All change-order costs arising from the allowance work during construction
options.C: Only the contractor's overhead and profit on the allowance materials
options.D: Only materials and equipment delivered to the site, including applicable taxes

questions.explanation: Under these standard general conditions, the cash allowance itself covers only the materials and equipment delivered to the site plus applicable taxes. The contractor's labor, handling, overhead, and profit are carried separately in the contract sum.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to bind actual agreement forms into the project manual rather than incorporating them by reference?

options.A: Because forms incorporated only by reference are not legally enforceable
options.B: To eliminate the risk of referencing an incorrect or out-of-date form
options.C: To make later editing of the agreement's terms by the A/E easier to do
options.D: To shorten the project manual by removing the bound contract forms

questions.explanation: Binding the actual agreement form into the project manual removes the danger of pointing to the wrong edition or an outdated version of the form, since everyone works from the exact document that is included.

questions.question: A self-adhering air barrier with an acrylic adhesive bonded to a PVC roof membrane is cited as an example of:

options.A: A successful manufacturer collaboration on the air-barrier assembly
options.B: An incompatibility likely to create a latent defect in the assembly
options.C: A properly coordinated basis-of-design pairing of barrier and membrane
options.D: A code-compliant prescriptive coordination of the roofing materials

questions.explanation: This pairing illustrates how two products chosen independently can turn out to be chemically or physically incompatible. If the mismatch is not caught before construction, it can become a hidden defect built into the assembly.

questions.question: Calling a fixture a 'service sink' in the specifications but a 'janitor's sink' on the drawings is an example of:

options.A: Acceptable industry variation in naming the same plumbing fixture across documents
options.B: Proper use of an approved alternative term sanctioned by the firm master specification
options.C: A deliberate cross-reference deliberately linking the specification and drawing schedule
options.D: Inconsistent terminology that causes confusion, higher costs, and construction delays

questions.explanation: Using two different names for the same fixture is exactly the kind of inconsistent terminology that confuses the reader. It can drive up costs, slow the work, and lead to mistakes in what gets installed.

questions.question: Why must fire-resistance-rated wall specifications closely match the tested assembly?

options.A: Because deviations from the products listed in the tested assembly are not permitted
options.B: Because performance criteria are allowed to override the prescriptive tested listing
options.C: Because the AHJ will accept any single listed manufacturer for the tested rating
options.D: Because the contractor is free to select any equivalent tested rated wall assembly

questions.explanation: A fire-resistance rating comes from a specific tested assembly built with specifically listed products. Swapping in products that were not part of that test breaks the basis for the rating, so deviations are generally not allowed.

questions.question: Where should a definition of basis-of-design products and acceptance of comparable products be included?

options.A: Only on the drawings
options.B: In the supplementary conditions
options.C: In Division 01
options.D: In each affected Division 02-49 section

questions.explanation: Because the definition of a basis-of-design product and the rules for accepting comparable products apply project-wide, they belong in Division 01 as a single common requirement rather than being repeated in every technical section.

questions.question: Coordination with sustainability consultants typically:

options.A: Is handled solely by the owner's commissioning agent during construction
options.B: Crosses all disciplines and is coordinated by the prime A/E of record
options.C: Is limited to the landscape and civil sections of the specifications
options.D: Falls to the structural engineer as the lead discipline for the project

questions.explanation: Sustainability requirements tend to touch every discipline rather than sitting in one trade. Pulling that cross-cutting input together is the prime A/E's responsibility as the party coordinating the overall specifications.

questions.question: Who holds the ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents?

options.A: The owner's representative
options.B: The A/E's project manager
options.C: The lead specifier
options.D: The general contractor

questions.explanation: Final accountability for coordinating the construction documents rests with the A/E's project manager. The PM can hand the task to another team member but still owns the responsibility for the result.

questions.question: Final coordination of construction documents should include verifying which of the following?

options.A: That the contractor has been pre-selected
options.B: Consistency of all schedules
options.C: Approval of substitution requests
options.D: That bidders have signed nondisclosure agreements

questions.explanation: Among the final checks before issuance is confirming that the schedules agree with one another and with the rest of the documents, alongside verifying that earlier-noted inconsistencies were fixed and the set is complete.

questions.question: Each technical specification section affected by an alternate should:

options.A: Restate the alternate's lump-sum price within Section 01 23 00 — Alternates
options.B: Include a PART 1 – GENERAL paragraph cross-referencing Section 01 23 00 – Alternates
options.C: Be physically separated from the base-bid sections into a Volume 2 alternate binder
options.D: Be withheld from the project manual until the owner selects that particular alternate

questions.explanation: A technical section touched by an alternate should flag that fact in its PART 1 – GENERAL text and point the reader to Section 01 23 00, so the connection between the technical scope and the listed alternate is explicit.

questions.question: Properly prepared drawings and specifications should:

options.A: Repeat the key requirements in both locations for added emphasis
options.B: Be prepared and issued under entirely separate prime contracts
options.C: Use identical wording in both documents throughout the set
options.D: Dovetail like a jigsaw puzzle, with no overlaps and no gaps

questions.explanation: Well-coordinated drawings and specifications interlock like puzzle pieces: each covers its own part of the requirements with no duplicated overlap and no missing gap between them.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the coordination process in construction project management?

options.A: To replace the need for formal design reviews by the team
options.B: To maximize the general contractor's overall profit margin
options.C: To centralize each and every project decision with the owner alone
options.D: To manage dependencies between project activities and parties

questions.explanation: Coordination adds value by managing how the many activities and parties on a project depend on one another. It counters the fragmentation that comes from numerous separate contributors each handling a piece of the work.

questions.question: When specifying liquidated damages, the specifier should tie the start of damages to:

options.A: The date the AHJ issues the certificate of occupancy for the completed work
options.B: The contractual substantial-completion date set in the conditions of the contract
options.C: The date the owner takes beneficial occupancy of the substantially finished building
options.D: The contractual final-completion date established in the owner-contractor agreement

questions.explanation: Liquidated damages are normally keyed to the contractual substantial-completion date defined in the conditions of the contract, not to final completion or to the day the owner happens to occupy the building.

questions.question: A product representative contacts the owner directly to push a preferred brand for the project. This action is:

options.A: Appropriate, provided the representative also copies the project A/E on the message
options.B: Appropriate, because the owner holds final product-selection authority on the project
options.C: Inappropriate, because it bypasses the design team and undermines impartial selection
options.D: Inappropriate only on publicly funded projects subject to competitive-bidding rules

questions.explanation: A product representative should route input through the A/E. Going straight to the owner sidesteps the design team and compromises the impartiality of the product-selection process.

questions.question: If inconsistent terminology appears in different specification sections, the most likely consequence is:

options.A: Confusion and conflicts during bidding and construction administration
options.B: A reduced overall sheet count in the project manual and drawings
options.C: Faster processing of contractor substitution requests by the A/E
options.D: Improved bidding competition through clearer scope for all the bidders

questions.explanation: When sections use different terms for the same thing, readers get confused during both bidding and construction administration. The mismatch tends to generate RFIs, change orders, and disputes over scope.

questions.question: When a fire-resistance-rated assembly is required, the specifications should reference:

options.A: Only the IBC fire-resistance table reference for the required rating
options.B: The contractor's preferred UL assembly carrying the same hourly rating
options.C: The specific tested UL design number matching the actual construction
options.D: Any UL design number that provides the required hourly fire rating

questions.explanation: A fire-rated assembly relies on the exact products listed in a particular tested design, and deviations are generally not permitted. The specification should therefore cite the specific tested design number that matches how the assembly is actually built, not just any listing with the same hourly rating.

questions.question: Hazardous-material removal on an existing building should be specified using:

options.A: A general note on the demolition drawings directing removal per available information
options.B: A reference in the conditions of the contract to the owner's hazmat consultant report by URL
options.C: Dedicated abatement sections coordinated with the bid form, work restrictions, and execution
options.D: A single Division 01 article that cross-references the applicable local building code

questions.explanation: Abatement work needs its own dedicated specification sections, coordinated with the bid form scope, the work restrictions, the sequencing, and the disposal requirements. A drawing note or a passing reference cannot carry that level of regulated detail.

questions.question: When a basis-of-design product is identified, listing both the product name AND the manufacturer's catalog number is:

options.A: Recommended, because it removes ambiguity for bidders and reviewers
options.B: Required only for owner-furnished items listed in Section 01 64 00
options.C: Prohibited under proprietary specification rules and fair competition
options.D: Unnecessary duplication that lengthens the section without benefit

questions.explanation: Naming both the product and its catalog number pins down exactly which item is meant, which matters when a manufacturer sells several similar variants under closely related names. The precision helps both bidders and reviewers.

questions.question: Which alternate labeling convention does CSI recommend to make the direction of price change unambiguous?

options.A: Use 'Choice 1' and 'Choice 2'
options.B: Use 'Alternative' instead of 'Alternate'
options.C: Use 'Add' and 'Deduct' alternates
options.D: Use 'Option A' and 'Option B'

questions.explanation: Labeling alternates as 'Add' or 'Deduct' states plainly whether selecting one raises or lowers the price. Generic labels like 'Option' or 'Choice' lose that information, and 'Alternative' is not the preferred term.

questions.question: The preferred CSI term for the construction documents' fixed scope priced by the bidder is:

options.A: Base bid
options.B: Baseline bid
options.C: Lump sum proposal
options.D: Initial offer

questions.explanation: The fixed scope a bidder prices is called the base bid; alternates are then added to or deducted from it. The preferred term is 'base bid' rather than 'baseline' or the other variants.

questions.question: Substantial completion was contractually due May 1. The work is substantially complete on May 15. The contract assesses $1,000 per calendar day of delay beginning the day after the deadline. The liquidated-damages assessment is:

options.A: $14,000 (counting May 2 through May 15 inclusive)
options.B: $16,000 (counting May 1 through May 16 inclusive)
options.C: $15,000 (counting May 1 through May 15 inclusive)
options.D: $13,000 (counting May 3 through May 15 inclusive)

questions.explanation: With the clock starting the day after the deadline, the delay runs from May 2 through May 15, which is 14 days. At $1,000 per day that totals $14,000. The stem states the accrual convention so the count is unambiguous.

questions.question: Toilet-accessory information on the architectural elevations conflicts with the accessory schedule. This should be resolved by:

options.A: Defaulting to whichever document shows the larger accessory quantity
options.B: Reconciling the discrepancy before issuance and citing one coordinated source
options.C: Letting the contractor choose which document to follow during construction
options.D: Issuing an RFI to resolve the conflict only well after the bids have been opened

questions.explanation: Conflicts among drawings, schedules, and specifications should be reconciled before the documents go out, so that a single coordinated source of truth governs. That prevents the ambiguity from reaching bidders.

questions.question: An owner has not furnished the insurance limits required for the supplementary conditions. The architect should MOST appropriately:

options.A: Adopt customary industry minimum limits and issue the documents without notice to the owner
options.B: Issue the project manual with the owner-furnished insurance-limit values left blank for entry
options.C: Direct the contractor to furnish proposed insurance limits during the bidding period itself
options.D: Request the limits from the owner in writing and hold the affected sections until furnished

questions.explanation: Setting insurance limits is the owner's responsibility, so the architect should not guess at them. The correct step is to request the values in writing and hold the affected sections until the owner provides them.

questions.question: An Invitation to Bidders states sealed bids will be received at a stated place and time. A bidder asks whether bids may be emailed. The correct answer is:

options.A: Yes, provided the emailed bid arrives before the stated deadline
options.B: No, unless the procurement documents expressly authorize an electronic method
options.C: No, because electronic delivery is never acceptable on any construction project
options.D: Yes, because electronic delivery is presumed acceptable under modern practice

questions.explanation: The procurement documents govern how bids may be submitted. A sealed-bid process does not permit emailed bids unless the instructions specifically authorize an electronic method.

questions.question: Which is the MOST appropriate purpose of identifying multiple procurement document distribution channels in the Invitation to Bidders?

options.A: To restrict bidders to the architect's preferred reprographer
options.B: To allow only invited bidders to access the documents
options.C: To eliminate the need for plan rooms
options.D: To broaden bidder access and competition

questions.explanation: Naming several places to obtain the documents (the A/E office, a reprographer, plan rooms, an online plan service) makes it easier for more prospective bidders to get them, which supports broader competition.

questions.question: An abatement specification states the contractor shall 'remove materials in accordance with industry practice.' This language is:

options.A: Acceptable, because abatement procedures are fully standardized by OSHA rules
options.B: Required to remain vague because the work is being performance-specified here
options.C: Insufficient, because it cites no specific standard, regulation, or procedure
options.D: Acceptable, because the term 'industry practice' is well-defined for abatement

questions.explanation: A phrase like 'industry practice' is too vague to enforce. Hazardous-material removal has to point to the specific regulation or procedure (such as the applicable EPA or OSHA standard) so the requirement is clear and enforceable.

questions.question: Two alternates each propose a different exterior cladding for one building elevation. The owner is MOST likely to:

options.A: Select neither alternate, since proposing two makes the base-bid scope ambiguous
options.B: Select at most one, because both alternates address one mutually exclusive scope
options.C: Select whichever alternate the low-bidding contractor recommends after award
options.D: Select both alternates so their installed performance can be compared post-award

questions.explanation: Two alternates covering the same scope are mutually exclusive, so the owner can pick at most one of them. The specifier should catch and flag such conflicts among proposed alternates before the documents go to bid.

questions.question: Owner-furnished, contractor-installed (OFCI) products require specific coordination because:

options.A: OFCI products are wholly exempt from the contractor's site coordination and storage duties
options.B: The owner purchases the OFCI product, but the contractor installs it and owns install quality
options.C: The contractor purchases the OFCI product while the owner inspects and accepts it on site
options.D: OFCI items must always be carried on the bid form as cash allowances priced by the contractor

questions.explanation: With OFCI items the responsibility is split: the owner buys the product (and usually holds its warranty), while the contractor installs it and remains accountable for the quality of that installation. Delivery, storage, and acceptance therefore have to be coordinated between the two.

questions.question: When two alternates are mutually exclusive (only one can be chosen), Section 01 23 00 – Alternates should:

options.A: Require the bidder to price both mutually exclusive alternates at the same amount
options.B: Delete one of the two alternates from Section 01 23 00 to simplify the bid form
options.C: Default to the lower-priced of the two alternates when the owner does not choose
options.D: State the mutually exclusive relationship and the priority for owner selection

questions.explanation: When alternates exclude one another, the Alternates section should say so and lay out the selection priority, so the bidder and owner both understand that only one can be chosen. The bid form should follow the same logic.

questions.question: A project manager assigns document-coordination duties to another design team member but keeps signing authority. Where does the ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents still reside?

options.A: With the assigned coordinating team member, who now owns the document outcome
options.B: With the independent specification consultant or manager preparing the project manual
options.C: With the architect/engineer's project manager, despite the delegation of the task
options.D: With each discipline lead individually for the sections that discipline prepared

questions.explanation: Final responsibility for coordinating the documents stays with the A/E's project manager. Delegating the hands-on work to another team member does not transfer that accountability.

questions.question: The recommended practice is to develop a preliminary project description or outline specifications early. The primary coordination value of that outline is that it:

options.A: Serves as a checklist that develops as design progresses
options.B: Fixes the project manual table of contents so it cannot later change
options.C: Replaces the need for additional coordination meetings
options.D: Establishes precedence of specifications over the drawings

questions.explanation: An early outline or preliminary project description works as a living checklist that grows and is refined as the design advances. It is a working coordination tool, not a frozen table of contents or a statement of precedence.

questions.question: Rather than placing overly specific catalog references on a drawing, designers should keep a separate list of catalog references and communicate it to the specifier. How should that list be organized?

options.A: By the design discipline that prepared each referenced detail
options.B: By an outline keyed to the project manual table of contents
options.C: Alphabetically by manufacturer name across all the disciplines
options.D: By the drawing sheet number on which each detail appears

questions.explanation: Such a list works best organized as an outline that follows the project manual table of contents. Matching the specification's order lets the specifier find the right references while writing each corresponding section.

questions.question: Among the final-coordination tasks before issuance is verifying that all previously noted inconsistencies are corrected and that the documents are complete. The third listed task is to verify the:

options.A: consistency of all schedules
options.B: precedence order stated in the conditions of the contract
options.C: insurance limits provided by the owner's adviser
options.D: allowance amounts carried in each Division 01 section

questions.explanation: The final coordination pass confirms that noted inconsistencies have been fixed, that the set is complete, and that all of the schedules are consistent with one another. The third of those tasks is verifying schedule consistency.

questions.question: An owner elects to furnish Division 01. To fulfill the A/E's contractual responsibilities, the A/E should:

options.A: Re-issue the owner's sections under the A/E's seal
options.B: Defer entirely to the owner's Division 01 and add nothing
options.C: Prepare additional Division 01 sections as necessary
options.D: Refuse the engagement until the owner relinquishes Division 01

questions.explanation: When the owner supplies Division 01, the A/E should still add whatever further Division 01 sections are needed to carry out its own contractual duties, coordinating them with the related sections, alternates, allowances, and unit prices.
questions.source: preliminary review of the project manual

questions.question: Standard specification practice distinguishes 'checking' from 'coordinating' the construction documents. A drawing that is internally correct but inconsistent with other documents illustrates a failure of:

options.A: Checking, because the drawing itself contains an error
options.B: Coordination, even though the drawing checks out alone
options.C: Precedence, because no priority order was stated
options.D: Terminology control across the disciplines

questions.explanation: Checking confirms a document is correct on its own; coordinating confirms it agrees with the other documents. A drawing that is right by itself yet clashes with another part of the set is a coordination failure, not a checking error.

questions.question: Two abbreviation tables in a drawing set list 'WT.' as both WEIGHT and WINDOW. The most direct consequence the A/E should anticipate from such inconsistency is that it can:

options.A: Shift document precedence to the specifications by default
options.B: Void the contractor's obligation to follow the drawings
options.C: Require the owner to issue the entire procurement documents again
options.D: Raise construction costs, cause delays, or cause faulty work

questions.explanation: An abbreviation that means two different things is exactly the inconsistent terminology that confuses readers. Left uncorrected it can push up costs, slow the schedule, and lead to work being built wrong.

questions.question: In a sample abbreviation legend, the existing condition is conveyed several different ways at once. Counting how many distinct ways one condition is shown is an exercise in:

options.A: Verifying contractor compliance with a tested fire-rated assembly
options.B: Coordinating allowance quantities with the project bid form prices
options.C: Establishing the order of precedence among all the contract documents
options.D: Enforcing consistent terminology and abbreviations across documents

questions.explanation: Tallying the different ways one condition is labeled makes the point about enforcing consistent terminology and abbreviations: using several labels for the same thing confuses the reader, which is the problem consistent terminology prevents.

questions.question: A curb detail labels the insulation only 'RIGID INSULATION,' while Section 07 21 00 lists three rigid types (XPS, polyiso, mineral wool). Based on the intended answer, the type to be installed is:

options.A: Unclear; the terminology must be coordinated
options.B: Polyisocyanurate, because it is foil-faced
options.C: Mineral wool, because it is noncombustible
options.D: Extruded polystyrene, because it is listed first

questions.explanation: A generic 'rigid insulation' note cannot be matched to any one of the three specified types, so it is impossible to tell which is intended. The terminology between the drawing and the specification needs to be coordinated.

questions.question: An engineer wants to add Section 22 00 05 - Firestopping for Plumbing because the architect already prepared 07 84 13 - Penetration Firestopping. The best-practice guidance is to:

options.A: Keep both sections so each discipline controls its own firestopping
options.B: Reference both sections from a Division 01 summary
options.C: Coordinate all firestopping into Division 07 under one section
options.D: Move all firestopping into the plumbing division for that trade

questions.explanation: Creating a second, duplicate firestopping section is not good practice. The plumbing firestopping requirements should be coordinated into the single Division 07 section so the same work is not specified two different ways.

questions.question: CSI's 'say it once and in the right place' principle exists chiefly to prevent which defect that an addendum is especially likely to create?

options.A: An allowance amount omitted from the bid form
options.B: A correction made in one location but missed in the duplicate
options.C: Use of an out-of-date standard agreement form
options.D: A precedence conflict between the drawings and specifications

questions.explanation: Duplicated requirements invite discrepancies because an addendum can fix one copy and overlook the other. Stating each requirement just once, in its proper place, removes the duplicate that an addendum might miss.

questions.question: Why is deviation from the listed products in a fire-resistance-rated assembly generally treated as impermissible?

options.A: Because product substitutions of listed products always increase the contract sum
options.B: Because the rating relies on a tested assembly of specifically listed products
options.C: Because Division 01 forbids any substitution to a listed assembly after contract award
options.D: Because only the building official may approve a change to a listed assembly

questions.explanation: The fire-resistance rating is earned by testing a particular assembly built from specifically listed products. Substituting products that were not in that test undermines the basis for the rating, so deviations are generally not allowed.

questions.question: A specification's owner-furnished article simply lists 'Soap Dispenser, Paper Towel Dispenser, Toilet Paper Dispenser' as owner-provided for the contractor to install. Is this sufficient for the contractor to bid?

options.A: No; the products are not identified well enough to price the install
options.B: Yes; owner-furnished items carry no installation cost to the bidder
options.C: Yes; the accessory schedule already lists the required install method
options.D: No; the only missing detail is the accessory manufacturer brand names

questions.explanation: Just naming the owner-furnished items is not enough to bid. Without identifying the products in enough detail, the contractor cannot reliably price the installation work, even though the owner is supplying the products themselves.

questions.question: A specification places the definition of basis-of-design and acceptance of comparable products in each technical section. Standard coordination guidance instead favors stating such common requirements:

options.A: In the invitation to bidders
options.B: In the conditions of the contract, Article 1
options.C: On sheet G-001, the drawing cover sheet
options.D: In the applicable Division 01 section

questions.explanation: Common requirements such as how comparable products and substitutions are handled belong in a single Division 01 section rather than being repeated in every technical section, which avoids the conflicting duplicates that repetition creates.

questions.question: Construction documents are nearly complete; the owner has repeatedly failed to provide the contractor's required insurance limits and tells the architect to 'use whatever you usually use.' The architect's BEST action is to:

options.A: Insert the insurance limits the architect used on a similar prior project file
options.B: Omit the owner's insurance limits from the documents entirely until provided
options.C: Request the owner confirm limits with their legal counsel and insurance agent
options.D: Set the limits at the highest amount any of the architect's past projects required

questions.explanation: Insurance limits are the owner's call, informed by the owner's own legal and insurance advisers. Rather than borrowing limits from another project or leaving them out, the architect should ask the owner to confirm the limits with their counsel and insurance agent.

questions.question: An owner's geotechnical report is needed by the A/E, its consultants, and the contractor. This report should be:

options.A: Referenced in Division 00 as Available Project Information
options.B: Issued only on request after the contract is signed
options.C: Attached to the agreement as a numbered contract exhibit
options.D: Bound into Division 01 as a general administrative requirement

questions.explanation: The owner is normally responsible for the geotechnical report, and it is provided to all parties by including or referencing it in Division 00 as available project information.

questions.question: The A/E should avoid incorporating the owner's standard agreement form by reference only. The principal reason is that binding the actual form into the project manual:

options.A: Removes the need to issue supplementary conditions with the agreement form
options.B: Allows the A/E to modify the bound agreement form's terms more conveniently
options.C: Transfers responsibility for the agreement form to the specification consultant
options.D: Eliminates the risk of referencing an incorrect or out-of-date agreement form

questions.explanation: Including the actual form rather than just pointing to it removes the chance of citing the wrong or an outdated edition, because the exact form everyone will use is bound right into the project manual.

questions.question: An owner's commissioning agent and security adviser will interact with the contractor during construction. The project specifications should therefore:

options.A: Name those owner's consultants as additional signatory parties to the agreement
options.B: Address the contractor's responsibilities in working with the owner's consultants
options.C: Exclude those owner's consultants because the owner, not the A/E, retained them
options.D: Shift coordination of those owner's consultants entirely onto the prime contractor

questions.explanation: Where the owner's consultants have duties that involve working with the contractor, the specifications should spell out the contractor's responsibilities in that interaction so the relationship is defined.

questions.question: A product representative, upset that proprietary language was edited out of a section, contacts the OWNER directly during bidding to complain. Contacting the owner was:

options.A: Inappropriate, and the A/E of record owns the project specifications
options.B: Appropriate, because the owner ultimately funds the entire project
options.C: Appropriate, since the rep authored the original guide specification
options.D: Inappropriate only when the project is a publicly funded contract

questions.explanation: Going directly to the owner was not appropriate. The specifications are the A/E of record's responsibility, and the A/E may properly edit a guide specification to open the section up to competition.

questions.question: On a CMAR or IPD project where the contractor is engaged early in design, the recommended practice is that the contractor should be:

options.A: Included in the project manual coordinating group
options.B: Given precedence over the A/E in resolving conflicts
options.C: Asked to prepare the procurement requirements
options.D: Limited to reviewing the drawings only

questions.explanation: When a delivery method like CMAR or IPD brings the contractor into the design stage, the contractor should be part of the group coordinating the project manual, since it is contributing while the documents are still being shaped.

questions.question: A curtain wall installer provides framing and glazing calculations and installation details to help develop the documents. This early involvement is identified as a:

options.A: A design-assist role contributing information to the specifications
options.B: A substitution request requiring formal A/E evaluation and approval
options.C: A value-analysis proposal submitted under Section 01 24 00 procedures
options.D: A voluntary alternate offered against the project's base-bid scope

questions.explanation: A subcontractor lending its expertise on one part of the design, such as an installer supplying calculations and installation details, is acting in a design-assist role that helps develop the documents.

questions.question: For multiple-prime work, the recommended practice is to use Section 01 12 00 - Multiple Contract Summary, which (unlike 01 11 00) must further define scope by including owner-furnished material and equipment to be installed and:

options.A: the order of precedence among the installed contract documents
options.B: the allowance amount carried for owner-furnished items in each package
options.C: by which contractor each owner-furnished item is to be installed
options.D: the liquidated-damages rate applied to each installed work package

questions.explanation: On multiple-prime work, Section 01 12 00 has to define scope by listing the owner-furnished material and equipment to be installed and identifying which contractor installs each item. That contractor-by-contractor breakdown is what distinguishes it from the single-contract 01 11 00.

questions.question: Per a coordination matrix, the specifier should coordinate primarily with which team member to verify whether a contractor has been selected and a contract is in place?

options.A: The owner
options.B: The consultant
options.C: The product representative
options.D: The architect/engineer

questions.explanation: Whether a contractor has been selected and a contract signed is something only the owner knows, because the owner holds that contractual relationship. So the specifier confirms it with the owner.

questions.question: Per a coordination matrix, identifying cost savings from an alternative design or construction technology is a task the specifier coordinates primarily with the:

options.A: The manufacturer's product representative
options.B: The owner's design consultant for that discipline
options.C: The prime architect/engineer of record
options.D: The owner's facility-management staff

questions.explanation: Cost savings from an alternative product or construction technology typically come from the product representative, who is the usual source for such design and construction alternatives.

questions.question: Two design team members independently select interfacing products that are not compatible, and the conflict is not caught before construction. The result this product-coordination role is meant to prevent is a:

options.A: voluntary alternate added to the base bid
options.B: quantity allowance overrun on the bid form
options.C: precedence dispute between drawings and specifications
options.D: latent defect built into the completed building

questions.explanation: If two interfacing products chosen separately are incompatible and nobody catches it before construction, the mismatch gets built in as a hidden, latent defect. Guarding against that outcome is the point of the specifier's product-coordination role.

questions.question: A specified accessory adhesive for a self-adhering air barrier may not maintain a bond with the adjacent membrane over time. Beyond coordinating a substitute adhesive with the architect, the recommended specifier action is to:

options.A: hold both sections unchanged until a field adhesive-bond test is performed
options.B: route the incompatible-adhesive issue to the contractor as a substitution request
options.C: replace the air-barrier membrane with an entirely different adhesive-free material
options.D: have the drawing notation revised once a compatible adhesive has been selected

questions.explanation: Two steps are called for: work with the architect to choose a more compatible adhesive, and once that compatible adhesive is settled, have the drawing notation updated so the documents reflect the corrected product.

questions.question: A fire-resistance design lists specific sprayed fire-resistive manufacturers; the spec's 'one of the following' list includes a manufacturer that is NOT named in the tested design. Per the intended answer, a base-bid product from that manufacturer is:

options.A: Not acceptable for that assembly, since it is absent from the tested design
options.B: Acceptable only if the contractor offers a five-percent price reduction at bid
options.C: Acceptable, because it appears in the specification's listed manufacturers
options.D: Acceptable if the architect waives the tested-design listing requirement at bid

questions.explanation: Because that manufacturer is not named in the tested fire-resistance design, its product is not acceptable for that indicated assembly, even though the specification's manufacturer list happens to include it. The tested design controls.

questions.question: During construction, a contractor submits a cost-saving substitution with documentation that the product is listed in a DIFFERENT tested assembly. Per the intended answer, the specifier should compare the proposed assembly to the specified tested design and:

options.A: Reject it outright because the manufacturer is not listed in the specified design
options.B: Forward it to the building official for that official's sole determination
options.C: Approve it if appropriate, assisting the architect in the evaluation
options.D: Approve it automatically on the basis of the owner's cost savings

questions.explanation: The specifier should compare the contractor's proposed tested assembly against the one specified and, if it is appropriate, approve it while assisting the architect. The request is neither rejected solely because of the manufacturer list nor approved on cost alone.

questions.question: For a climate zone with a given projection factor and glazing not yet selected, the recommended specifier action is to incorporate language requiring glazing to:

options.A: meet or exceed the minimum standards of the energy conservation code
options.B: have a fixed solar heat gain coefficient of exactly 0.40 regardless of frame
options.C: match the U-factor of the climate-zone-5 curtain wall on a similar project
options.D: be selected later by the contractor to control the project's overall cost

questions.explanation: With the glazing still undecided, the specification should require it to meet or exceed the minimum energy conservation code standards rather than locking in a single numeric value too early, which keeps the requirement correct whatever glazing is ultimately chosen.

questions.question: Sustainability requirements on a project cut across the mechanical, electrical, and architectural sections. Coordination of the sustainability consultant's input should be handled by the:

options.A: the sustainability consultant inputting directly into each discipline's section
options.B: the prime A/E, who coordinates the input that crosses all of the disciplines
options.C: the owner's commissioning agent gathering the input during the construction stage
options.D: the contractor, who collects the input once the work packages have been issued

questions.explanation: Sustainability input spans multiple disciplines, so the prime A/E, who is responsible for the overall coordination of the specifications, should be the one pulling that cross-cutting input together.

questions.question: Coordinating multiple-package documents runs in both directions. A common pitfall is that a change made in a LATER package, affecting work already issued earlier, is the case most easily overlooked unless it is:

options.A: deferred to a post-award change order
options.B: absorbed within the earlier package's price
options.C: back-coordinated into the earlier package
options.D: governed by a stated precedence order

questions.explanation: Carrying early-package changes forward into later packages is intuitive, but the reverse is easy to miss: a change introduced in a later package that affects already-issued work must be back-coordinated into the earlier package to keep everything consistent.

questions.question: When mechanical engineers each insert a 'Submittal Procedures' section into their own divisions, the coordination guidance for the Division 01 lead is to:

options.A: permit each division to keep its own submittal procedures
options.B: relocate submittal procedures from Division 01 to the conditions
options.C: fold the unique elements into the common Division 01 section
options.D: delete the engineers' added sections without any discussion

questions.explanation: Duplicate submittal-procedure sections conflict with the common Division 01 section. The reviewer should figure out what unique requirement prompted each separate section and merge those elements into the single Division 01 submittal section.

questions.question: An abatement consultant's Section 02 82 13 directs both the 'Abatement Contractor' and the 'window replacement contractor' to perform parts of the work. Naming a second contractor in this section is:

options.A: appropriate, because it clarifies the specialist interface for the second contractor
options.B: not appropriate, because one section must not assign work to another contractor
options.C: appropriate only when both named contractors sign the very same prime agreement
options.D: not appropriate unless the owner is self-performing the window-replacement work

questions.explanation: A specification section should not hand work to a separate contractor. Directing the window-replacement contractor inside the abatement section is not appropriate; that kind of cross-contractor coordination belongs in Division 01 and the broader contract documents.

questions.question: Questions of precedence often arise between drawings and specifications. The construction documents are designed to be:

options.A: ranked by precedence, with the specifications always controlling the drawings
options.B: sealed separately by precedence, so each discipline document governs itself
options.C: complementary, so a precedence statement in the project manual is not needed
options.D: phased by precedence, so the most recently issued document automatically governs

questions.explanation: Although precedence questions come up, the documents are meant to complement one another. For that reason a precedence statement is not recommended, and a conflict is settled instead by an A/E interpretation.

questions.question: Before final payment on work covered by a cash allowance, the contract sum is reconciled to actual cost by:

options.A: a deductive change applied to the bid bond amount for the cost difference
options.B: a supplementary condition issued at closeout reconciling the allowance cost
options.C: an appropriate change order reflecting the allowance's cost difference
options.D: a unit-price adjustment recorded on the proposal form for the cost variance

questions.explanation: The allowance provisions call for adjusting the contract sum by change order to capture the difference between the allowance amount and the actual cost, with that change order issued before final payment.

questions.question: There is one narrow exception to the rule against precedence listings: a precedence listing may be prepared:

options.A: for bidding purposes only
options.B: for warranty enforcement after closeout
options.C: whenever the owner furnishes the general conditions
options.D: only on multiple-prime contracts

questions.explanation: Precedence listings are generally discouraged, with one limited exception: if needed, a precedence listing may be prepared for bidding purposes only.

questions.question: An abatement spec article directs a 'fine spray mist' applied until the material is 'sufficiently saturated, without causing excess dripping.' This execution language is:

options.A: clear, because the article cites both the OSHA and the NESHAP standards
options.B: clear, because the wetting and spray equipment is specified for the work
options.C: not clear, because it relies on vague, unmeasurable removal terminology
options.D: not clear only if the asbestos-containing material type is omitted here

questions.explanation: Phrases like 'fine spray mist' and 'sufficiently saturated' give the contractor no measurable benchmark to follow, so the procedure is not clear. Execution language for regulated work needs a definite, measurable standard.

questions.question: In an abatement section, one statement directs removal of all asbestos-containing material on the inventory/plans, and another directs removal of non-friable Transite panels with wetting. These two statements are best described as:

options.A: in conflict, because both statements address the same asbestos removal scope
options.B: out of place, because both statements belong in PART 1 — GENERAL instead
options.C: redundant, so the statement covering the Transite panels should be deleted
options.D: complementary, addressing different aspects of the asbestos removal work

questions.explanation: One statement defines the scope of material to be removed while the other gives the method for the non-friable Transite. They cover different aspects of the same job and so are complementary rather than conflicting.

questions.question: A demolition section states hazardous materials shall be removed 'in accordance with Document 00 31 26 - Existing Hazardous Material Information.' This is inappropriate chiefly because Document 00 31 26 is:

options.A: information that the selective-demolition section supersedes as a contract document
options.B: information provided for the bidder and is not itself a contract document
options.C: information given in a Division 01 section that cannot govern Division 02 work
options.D: information tied to an allowance whose abatement scope must be priced apart

questions.explanation: That document is furnished for the bidder's information and is expressly not a contract document. Work cannot be made part of the contract simply by referencing such informational material; abatement scope must be specified in its own enforceable sections.

questions.question: A liquidated-damages clause, per the UCC discussion, is enforceable when the amount is reasonable and verifiable, but is UNENFORCEABLE when the amount is:

options.A: stated per calendar day rather than per working day
options.B: smaller than the owner's actual proven loss
options.C: excessive and unsubstantiated
options.D: tied to substantial completion rather than final completion

questions.explanation: Liquidated damages hold up when the daily amount is a reasonable, supportable estimate of the owner's loss. If the figure is excessive and cannot be substantiated, it reads as a penalty and the clause becomes unenforceable.

questions.question: A contract sets liquidated damages at $750 per calendar day. Substantial completion was due April 10 and was achieved April 25, with damages running the day after the deadline through the date achieved. The amount assessed is:
questions.explanation: Counting from April 11 through April 25 inclusive gives 15 days of delay. At $750 per day, 15 × $750 = $11,250. The damages run from the day after the deadline through the date substantial completion was reached.

questions.question: An Invitation to Bidders provides that bids will be received sealed at a stated office and then 'publicly opened and read aloud.' A bidder proposes to email its bid instead. Emailing must be refused mainly because it would defeat the requirement that bids be:

options.A: notarized and sealed by the bidder, then opened privately before the deadline
options.B: received only from the prime bidder in person, at the stated office, never read aloud
options.C: accompanied by a separately sealed alternate price envelope, opened publicly
options.D: received sealed and then opened publicly and read aloud at one stated time

questions.explanation: The Invitation provides for sealed bids that are then opened publicly and read aloud at a single set time. An emailed bid cannot satisfy that sealed-and-publicly-opened process, so it must be refused.

questions.question: An Invitation to Bidders says printed documents may be purchased from one print shop, and may also be reviewed at three other named locations. In addition to the print shop, how many places are listed where documents may be obtained or reviewed?

options.A: One additional location besides the print shop
options.B: Four additional locations besides the print shop site
options.C: Two additional locations besides the print shop
options.D: Three additional locations besides the print shop

questions.explanation: Beyond the print shop, three more locations are named where the documents can be reviewed, giving three additional places.

questions.question: The Invitation states a Performance Bond and a Payment Bond will be required in the amount of 100% of the Contract Price. If the contract price is $4 million, the bond amount required is:

options.A: $4 million
options.B: $6 million
options.C: None
options.D: $8 million

questions.explanation: When the bonds are required at 100 percent of the contract price, a $4 million contract requires bonds of $4 million.

questions.question: An open pre-bid meeting states 'Prime Bidders interested in submitting a bid are required to attend.' A tile SUBcontractor interested in bidding to the primes asks if attendance is mandatory. The tile subcontractor is:

options.A: required to attend, the same as the prime bidders and all interested bidders
options.B: required to attend only when no prime bidder will represent the tile scope
options.C: not required to attend, because the requirement names only the prime bidders
options.D: not required to attend only when the pre-bid meeting of bidders is virtual

questions.explanation: The mandatory-attendance language is directed at prime bidders. A tile subcontractor is not a prime bidder, so it is not required to attend.

questions.question: Section 01 21 00 - Allowances should identify both items covered by an allowance and cost items NOT covered. The purpose of this second list is so that, for example, delivery, installation, overhead, and profit are:

options.A: deducted from the cash allowance at closeout
options.B: included in the contract sum rather than the allowance
options.C: priced as separate unit prices on the bid form
options.D: carried as a contingency in the conditions of the contract

questions.explanation: Listing the costs an allowance does not cover (delivery, handling, installation, overhead, profit, and the like) makes clear that those costs belong in the contract sum, not in the allowance amount.

questions.question: A device whose final installed COUNT is unknown but whose make-up is fully defined (e.g., 55 corridor entrances of a specified door/frame/hardware set) is best handled in Division 01 as a:

options.A: cash allowance in Section 01 21 13
options.B: voluntary alternate in Section 01 23 00
options.C: value-analysis item in Section 01 24 00
options.D: quantity allowance in Section 01 21 19

questions.explanation: This is a quantity allowance: the assembly is fully defined but the installed count is only estimated, with unit prices used to true up the sum as the actual quantity varies. Section 01 21 19 covers quantity allowances.

questions.question: Estimated quantities for unit-price items are placed on the bid/proposal form rather than in the unit-price specification section because those quantities:

options.A: are guaranteed minimum quantities the contractor must furnish
options.B: establish precedence over the drawings for field measurement
options.C: determine the liquidated-damages daily rate for the project
options.D: are estimates for comparing bids and setting the contract sum

questions.explanation: The quantities are estimates, not guarantees. They exist so bids can be compared on a common basis and the contract sum determined, while actual payment is based on the work performed and measured in the field.

questions.question: Which scenario most clearly calls for a UNIT PRICE rather than an allowance or an alternate?

options.A: The owner may delete the entry canopy if bids exceed the set budget
options.B: Rock excavation volume is unknown until digging, priced per cubic yard
options.C: The owner wants a separate add price to install rooftop solar later
options.D: A selected light fixture's make is undecided, so a cash sum is carried

questions.explanation: Unit prices fit work whose exact quantity is unknown until it is performed, with the sum adjusted by a per-unit rate, such as rock excavation paid per cubic yard. An undecided product carried as a cash sum is an allowance, and add/deduct scope priced separately is an alternate.

questions.question: Which document must accurately reflect WHICH alternates the owner actually selected so they become part of the work?

options.A: The invitation to bidders
options.B: The executed agreement
options.C: Section 01 23 00 - Alternates
options.D: The instructions to bidders

questions.explanation: While Section 01 23 00 describes the available alternates, it is the executed agreement that records which ones the owner actually chose, stating them as part of the work description with the contract sum adjusted to match.

questions.question: Section 01 23 00 contains two alternates that both apply to the SAME exterior surface, each proposing a different cladding, making them mutually exclusive. The owner would:

options.A: not select both, since the two cladding alternates are mutually exclusive
options.B: convert both mutually exclusive alternates into unit prices for the surface
options.C: select both mutually exclusive alternates to maximize the cladding variety
options.D: merge the two mutually exclusive alternates into one combined deduct alternate

questions.explanation: Since both alternates govern the same surface, only one of them can be applied. The owner would not pick both, because the two are mutually exclusive.

questions.question: Reviewing draft alternate documents, the PREFERRED terminology pair is:

options.A: 'Baseline' and 'Alternative'
options.B: 'Base/base bid' and 'Alternative'
options.C: 'Baseline' and 'Alternate'
options.D: 'Base/base bid' and 'Alternate'

questions.explanation: The preferred CSI terms are 'base' or 'base bid' (not 'baseline') paired with 'alternate' (not 'alternative'). That pairing is the standard terminology.

questions.question: If an alternate's extent is NOT shown on the drawings, the alternate description may instead:

options.A: transfer the alternate's pricing into the instructions to bidders instead
options.B: describe the areas or portions of work to clarify the change locations
options.C: establish the alternate's order of precedence over the project's base bid
options.D: state the add or deduct dollar amount carried for the alternate in the bid

questions.explanation: When the drawings do not depict the alternate's extent, the description can identify the affected areas or portions of work in words, so bidders understand where the change caused by the alternate applies.

questions.question: Under the AIA A201 and ConsensusDocs 200 Allowances articles, the cash allowance included in the contract sum is limited to:

options.A: Only the contractor's unloading, handling, and installation labor at the site
options.B: All labor, material, overhead, profit, and the contractor's site handling costs
options.C: Materials and equipment delivered to the site, including the applicable taxes
options.D: Materials, installation, overhead, and profit for a complete finished installation

questions.explanation: Under these standard provisions the cash allowance covers only the materials and equipment delivered to the site, including applicable taxes. The contractor's unloading, handling, installation labor, overhead, and profit are carried in the contract sum unless stated otherwise.

questions.question: The documents coordinating an allowance must specify all of the following EXCEPT:

options.A: Precisely what scope of work is included under the stated allowance
options.B: Who is to authorize the items that are covered by the allowance
options.C: How costs adjust if actual price, quantity, or time varies from the amount
options.D: Which single manufacturer's product the allowance amount must purchase

questions.explanation: The coordinated documents must state what the allowance includes, who authorizes the allowance items, and how costs adjust when the actual price, quantity, or time differs. They do not lock the allowance to one mandatory manufacturer's product.

questions.question: On a stipulated-sum contract that lists a few unit prices, the estimated quantities shown on the bid form are best understood as:

options.A: Guaranteed maximums that the contractor may not exceed without a change order
options.B: The basis for comparing bids, with payment made for work actually performed
options.C: Cash allowances folded into the contract sum and reconciled at final payment
options.D: Fixed lump-sum quantities establishing the entire contract price at award only

questions.explanation: Bid-form quantities are estimates used to compare bids on a common footing and to set the contract sum. Payment is made for the work actually performed and measured, and the sum is later adjusted by change order to reflect real quantities.

questions.question: A site-utilities item has a unit cost that can be fixed at bid, but its total quantity is unknown until the work is measured in place. This is best handled as:

options.A: A cash allowance carried in Section 01 21 00 — Allowances
options.B: A supplementary condition fixing a lump-sum price for the item
options.C: A deduct alternate described in Section 01 23 00 — Alternates
options.D: A unit price established in Section 01 27 00 — Unit Prices

questions.explanation: When the price per unit is known but the total quantity is uncertain until measured, a unit price is the right tool. Section 01 27 00 — Unit Prices sets up the procedures, and the contract sum is adjusted by change order for the measured quantity.

questions.question: Which document must indicate, as part of the work description, exactly which alternates the owner has selected?

options.A: The instructions to bidders within the procurement requirements description
options.B: The executed owner-contractor agreement, as part of the work description
options.C: Section 01 23 00 — Alternates, among the project's Division 01 sections
options.D: The supplementary conditions the owner uses to modify general conditions

questions.explanation: The executed agreement is where the selected alternates are recorded as part of the work description, with the contract sum reflecting those choices. Standard general conditions usually need no change, because chosen alternates simply become part of the work.

questions.question: When alternates are used, modification of the standard general conditions is:

options.A: Generally required to add alternate pricing and selection rules to the contract
options.B: Always required, since alternates change the parties' rights and remedies
options.C: Required only on public projects subject to competitive-bidding statutes
options.D: Generally not required, because selected alternates become part of the work

questions.explanation: Alternates usually do not require changing the standard general conditions, because once the owner selects an alternate listed in the agreement form it simply becomes part of the work.

questions.question: In a Division 02-49 technical section affected by an allowance, the paragraph calling attention to the allowance provisions belongs in:

options.A: PART 2 — PRODUCTS, beside the allowance product's basis-of-design listing
options.B: PART 3 — EXECUTION, with the installation and field-quality text
options.C: PART 1 — GENERAL, cross-referencing the Division 01 allowance amount
options.D: A Division 01 appendix bound separately from the affected technical section

questions.explanation: A technical section touched by an allowance should flag the allowance in its PART 1 — GENERAL text and point to the allowance amount stated in the applicable Division 01 section, keeping the cross-reference in the general administrative part of the section.

questions.question: Duplicating a requirement in both the drawings and the specifications is risky chiefly because:

options.A: It violates the MasterFormat rule against repeating section numbers
options.B: Duplicated text may always increase the printed project manual page count
options.C: The specifications would then automatically take precedence over drawings
options.D: An addendum may correct one location and overlook the duplicate elsewhere

questions.explanation: The specifications should complement the drawings rather than repeat them. When a requirement appears in both, an addendum for a design change can fix one copy and miss the other, leaving a discrepancy that breeds conflicting interpretations, change orders, and added cost.

questions.question: Because the drawings and specifications are complementary, the recommended practice is for the conditions of the contract to address a conflict between them by providing that:

options.A: The A/E makes a documented interpretation that resolves the document conflict
options.B: The most recently issued of the two conflicting documents always controls
options.C: The contractor selects the more stringent of the conflicting requirements to use
options.D: The specifications govern the drawings in any conflict between the two documents

questions.explanation: Because the documents complement one another, precedence statements are discouraged. The conditions should simply provide that, when the drawings and specifications conflict, the A/E resolves it with a documented interpretation.

questions.question: The specifier is the default coordinator of products and materials. This role means the specifier:

options.A: Overrides any design-team product choice the specifier judges to be unsuitable
options.B: Is the sole decision-maker selecting every one of the products and materials used
options.C: Approves all contractor substitutions in place of the construction administrator
options.D: Confirms products are used as intended and are compatible with adjacent ones

questions.explanation: As the default product coordinator the specifier is not the sole decision-maker. The role is to act as the final check that products are applied as intended and remain compatible with the materials next to them.

questions.question: Why should Section 01 21 00 — Allowances identify the cost items NOT covered by an allowance?

options.A: To shift those excluded costs onto the owner's separate cash account
options.B: To document those excluded items for the owner's later unit-price claim
options.C: To convert the excluded items into a deduct alternate at the owner's option
options.D: To ensure those excluded costs are still included in the contract sum

questions.explanation: Spelling out the costs an allowance does not cover, such as delivery, storage and handling, installation, overhead, and profit, ensures those costs are still captured in the contract sum rather than being overlooked.

questions.question: The ultimate responsibility for coordinating the construction documents is assigned to:

options.A: The independent specification consultant preparing the project manual
options.B: The owner's construction manager, who may oversee the design phase
options.C: The A/E's project manager, who delegates the task but keeps responsibility
options.D: Each discipline lead, taking responsibility independently for its own sections

questions.explanation: Final responsibility for coordinating the construction documents sits with the A/E's project manager. The PM may assign the hands-on work to another team member, but the responsibility itself stays with the PM.

questions.question: Section 01 27 00 — Unit Prices must, among other things, define:

options.A: Who is responsible for measuring unit-price quantities and how it is verified
options.B: The estimated quantities, which are simply duplicated from the bid or proposal form
options.C: The guaranteed total contract sum, independent of the measured quantities
options.D: The single lump-sum price for all unit-price items combined on the project

questions.explanation: The unit-price section must say who measures the quantities and how that is verified: if the owner measures, the administrative procedures are defined, and if the contractor measures, the owner's methods for controlling and confirming the results are specified. The estimated quantities live on the bid form, not in this section.

questions.question: On a fast-track project issued in multiple packages, coordination between packages requires that:

options.A: Only the very final package incorporates all of the accumulated earlier modifications
options.B: Early-package modifications carry forward, with later changes back-coordinated
options.C: Each package stands fully alone, with no carryover of any earlier modifications
options.D: All packages are held and issued together once every change has been finalized

questions.explanation: Coordination across packages runs both ways: modifications made in early packages must be carried into the later ones, and a change introduced in a later package has to be back-coordinated into the earlier packages so the whole set stays consistent.

questions.question: Performance-type green requirements where means and methods are left to the contractor would best appear in:

options.A: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals and design records
options.B: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures for design data
options.C: Section 01 81 13—Sustainable Design Requirements
options.D: Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices for sustainable products

questions.explanation: Where a sustainability target is written as a performance outcome and the contractor is free to decide how to reach it, the right home for that requirement is the sustainable design section, 01 81 13. The other listed sections handle closeout records, submittal logistics, or pricing rather than green performance goals.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, how are shop drawings, product data, and samples best characterized?

options.A: Procurement requirements that become enforceable upon execution of the owner-contractor agreement
options.B: Contract documents that, once reviewed, bind the owner to the means and methods shown
options.C: Contract documents only for the portions of the work that are delegated-design submittals
options.D: Not contract documents; they show how the contractor proposes to meet the design intent

questions.explanation: A201 treats these submittals as something other than contract documents. They exist to show the way the contractor intends to satisfy the design intent, so reviewing them does not transfer responsibility for the design to the reviewer or make the submittals part of the contract.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, addenda must be issued by what point?

options.A: Before the time of substantial completion
options.B: Before receipt of bids
options.C: Before execution of the agreement
options.D: Before the pre-construction meeting
