questions.explanation: EJCDC, geared toward public works, treats an addendum as a pre-bid instrument: it must go out before bids are received. That reflects the public-procurement rule against altering the documents once bidding has closed but the contract is not yet signed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a standardized RFI form in the project manual?

options.A: It eliminates the need for change orders during construction
options.B: It substitutes for the contractor's required schedule of values document
options.C: It provides spaces for both the interpretation request and the response
options.D: It replaces the need for formal shop drawing review by the A/E

questions.explanation: A pre-printed RFI form streamlines clarifications by giving the requester room to state the question and the A/E room to answer it on the same document. Including it in the project manual keeps the question-and-answer process orderly.

questions.question: Which Division 01 section aligns with PART 2—PRODUCTS of SectionFormat?

options.A: Administrative Requirements
options.B: Product Requirements
options.C: Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.D: Quality Control (Field)

questions.explanation: SectionFormat's PART 2 deals with products, so the Division 01 groups that parallel it concern product and performance requirements and source-based quality control. Administrative and quality-assurance content instead lines up with PART 1—GENERAL.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, a field order is:

options.A: An engineer's directive used only when price and time changes cannot yet be agreed upon
options.B: A written order by the owner that always extends the contract time for the changed work
options.C: A written order by the engineer for minor changes not affecting contract price or time
options.D: An owner-signed instrument required before a formal change order can be executed

questions.explanation: In the EJCDC system a field order lets the engineer direct small changes in writing without touching the contract price or the contract time. Because nothing financial or scheduling changes, it needs neither the owner's signature nor a full change order.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the architect's review of submittals is for the limited purpose of:

options.A: Approving the contractor's means, methods, sequences, and safety precautions
options.B: Determining the accuracy and completeness of all dimensions and quantities shown
options.C: Substantiating the contractor's installation and equipment-performance instructions
options.D: Checking conformance with information given and the design concept

questions.explanation: A201 narrows the architect's submittal review to one thing: confirming that what is submitted lines up with the information furnished and with the overall design concept in the contract documents. It is not a check of dimensions, quantities, means, or methods.
questions.source: submittal review under the general conditions

questions.question: In EJCDC procurement documents, the manufacturer or vendor furnishing the goods is referred to as:

options.A: The Seller
options.B: The Contractor
options.C: The Subcontractor
options.D: The Manufacturer of Record

questions.explanation: EJCDC purchasing documents use commercial-sale vocabulary: the party supplying the goods is the Seller and the owner is the Buyer. The term 'work,' typical of construction agreements, is not used in these goods documents.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the substitution review process under Section 01 25 00?

options.A: To determine whether a proposed product is equivalent to the specified product
options.B: To document the basis for an automatic extension of the contract time
options.C: To establish the unit price adjustment when quantities differ from estimates
options.D: To transfer responsibility for product selection from the A/E to the contractor

questions.explanation: The substitution section sets out the ground rules for evaluating a contractor's proposed alternative, the central question being whether the offered product is genuinely equivalent to what was specified. It does not shift selection responsibility or adjust time or unit prices.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the procurement requirements in the project manual?

options.A: They restate Division 01 provisions so that bidders remain bound during construction
options.B: They take precedence over the general conditions in any conflict of requirements
options.C: They become contract documents automatically once bids are opened and tabulated
options.D: They are not contract documents and are unenforceable during contract administration

questions.explanation: Across the major standard general conditions, procurement requirements sit outside the contract documents. Anything stated only there governs the bidding phase and cannot be enforced once the project moves into construction administration.

questions.question: Estimated unit price quantities listed on the bid form are best described as:

options.A: Guaranteed minimum quantities for which the contractor will be paid in full
options.B: Estimates used to compare bids; payment is for work actually performed
options.C: Cash allowances included in the contract sum for the listed unit-price items
options.D: Maximum quantities that the contractor is contractually barred from exceeding

questions.explanation: The quantities printed on the bid form are only estimates that let bids be compared on a common basis and a contract sum to be set. The contractor is ultimately paid for the quantity actually installed and measured, not for the estimate.

questions.question: Which Division 01 section addresses BOTH contract-modification procedures and the RFI clarification process?

options.A: Section 01 32 00—Construction Progress Documentation
options.B: Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices and pricing procedures
options.C: Section 01 26 00—Contract Modification Procedures
options.D: Section 01 75 00—Starting and Adjusting procedures

questions.explanation: The contract modification section is where the documents set up a way for either party to ask for a clarification through an RFI and for the A/E to answer it without altering the contract sum or time. The other sections cover documentation, pricing, or startup.

questions.question: Which CSI principle is preserved by the relationship between Division 01 and other specification sections?

options.A: Say it once and in the right place
options.B: Keep all requirements general
options.C: State it twice for emphasis
options.D: Repeat across all sections for clarity

questions.explanation: By collecting the shared administrative and procedural rules in one place rather than scattering them through every technical section, Division 01 embodies the idea of stating a requirement a single time in its proper location.

questions.question: An RFI is appropriately used when:

options.A: An item of work is insufficiently described or detailed in the contract documents
options.B: The contractor seeks to add scope and a corresponding increase in the contract sum
options.C: The contractor is preparing its periodic application for payment for completed work
options.D: A product substitution is proposed by the contractor after the contract is awarded

questions.explanation: The proper trigger for an RFI is a gap or ambiguity in the documents that needs interpretation. The resulting answer clarifies intent without changing the contract sum or time, so it is not the vehicle for added scope, payment, or substitutions.

questions.question: Overspecifying in Division 01 most likely results in:

options.A: Faster A/E review of contractor submittals
options.B: Reduced contractor change orders and claims
options.C: Unnecessarily increased construction costs
options.D: Improved coordination among the trades on site

questions.explanation: Loading Division 01 with more than a project needs tends to drive up the cost of construction and saddles the party administering the contract with obligations that add little value.

questions.question: When multiple-prime contracts are used, which Division 01 section is most likely required instead of (or in addition to) Section 01 11 00?

options.A: Section 01 12 00—Multiple Contract Summary
options.B: Section 01 35 00—Special Procedures
options.C: Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices
options.D: Section 01 79 00—Demonstration and Training

questions.explanation: When the work is split among several contracts, as with multiple-prime arrangements, construction management, or some design-build setups, the multiple contract summary section is used to describe how those separate contracts fit together.

questions.question: In the three-party construction-bond relationship, the surety is only secondarily liable. The primary obligation to perform belongs to which party?

options.A: The contractor, as principal under the bond
options.B: The owner, who is the obligee on the bond
options.C: The architect/engineer who designed it
options.D: The subcontractors and the material suppliers

questions.explanation: A bond is not insurance: the surety steps in only after the principal fails. The contractor, as principal, carries the primary duty to perform and must reimburse the surety for any loss the surety pays out.

questions.question: Section 01 14 00—Work Restrictions is primarily intended to address:

options.A: Schedule of values and payment-application requirements
options.B: Requirements for independent testing laboratories
options.C: Limitations on the contractor's use of the premises
options.D: Construction progress photographs and documentation

questions.explanation: The work restrictions section places limits on how the contractor may use the site, which matters most when the building remains occupied during the work. Owner protection, access, and similar topics belong to other Division 01 sections.

questions.question: Under delegated design in AIA A201, the owner and architect are entitled to:

options.A: Receive a royalty or fee share from the delegated design professional's services
options.B: Independently redesign the delegated portion and back-charge the contractor for it
options.C: Reject every submittal originating from the delegated design professional without cause
options.D: Rely on the adequacy and completeness of the delegated professional's certifications

questions.explanation: When the documents call for the contractor to furnish professional design services and supply the related certifications, A201 lets the owner and architect treat those services and certifications as reliable, complete, and accurate rather than re-checking them.
questions.source: delegated design under the general conditions

questions.question: Section 01 25 00—Substitution Procedures should address substitutions during which time frame(s)?

options.A: Only during the procurement (bidding) stage, before the contract is awarded
options.B: Only after contract award, since procurement substitutions go through addenda
options.C: Only after substantial completion, as part of closeout and warranty resolution
options.D: Both procurement and after contract award, where each phase allows them

questions.explanation: A single substitution section can carry the rules for both the bidding stage and the post-award stage when substitutions are permitted in each. The procurement documents then simply point to that section rather than repeating the procedure.

questions.question: Including 'Basic Requirements' or 'Special Provisions' sections within individual technical divisions is:

options.A: Preferred when Division 01 is incomplete, since it may fill procedural gaps
options.B: Required by MasterFormat whenever a division contains more than one section
options.C: Not recommended, because such sections can create conflicts with Division 01
options.D: Mandatory on multiple-prime projects to assign division-specific responsibilities

questions.explanation: Tucking general-purpose 'basic requirements' or 'special provisions' sections into individual technical divisions is discouraged, since the procedural language there can collide with what Division 01 already states.

questions.question: Section 01 25 00 should also include procedures for substitution of:

options.A: A specified installer
options.B: The surety company
options.C: The owner's representative
options.D: The architect/engineer of record

questions.explanation: Substitutions are not limited to products. The section should also spell out how a request to use an installer other than the one specified is to be handled.

questions.question: Which instrument is commonly used to accept substitutions after the owner-contractor agreement is executed?

options.A: Bid bond furnished with the bidder's proposal
options.B: Schedule of values submitted with the application
options.C: Addendum issued before the agreement is signed
options.D: Change order, the ConsensusDocs 202 form

questions.explanation: Once the agreement is signed, changes to the work, including accepting a substitution, are formalized through a change order, which also records any adjustment to price and time. An addendum can no longer be used at that point because it is a pre-signing instrument.

questions.question: How many days before receipt of bids does AIA A701 require bidder questions to be submitted?

options.A: At least 14 days
options.B: At least 10 days
options.C: At least 4 days
options.D: At least 7 days

questions.explanation: AIA's Instructions to Bidders sets a minimum of seven days before bids are received for bidder questions to come in. The comparable EJCDC recommendation is a longer window of about ten days.

questions.question: Which Division 01 section establishes general submittal procedures?

options.A: Section 01 78 00—Closeout Submittals procedures
options.B: Section 01 33 00—Submittal Procedures
options.C: Section 01 31 00—Project Management and Coordination
options.D: Section 01 40 00—Quality Requirements and procedures

questions.explanation: The general rules for submittals, including the submittal schedule, shop drawings, product data, samples, sustainable-design reporting, formatting, and required copies, are set in Section 01 33 00.

questions.question: Under the FAR Buy American restriction, for non-iron/steel construction materials, the cost of domestic components must generally exceed what percentage of all components?

options.A: 95 percent
options.B: 55 percent
options.C: 75 percent
options.D: 25 percent

questions.explanation: For construction materials that are not predominantly iron or steel, the FAR Buy American rule generally requires that more than 55 percent of total component cost be domestic. The separate iron-and-steel test instead caps foreign content at under five percent.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the contractor is generally not obligated to furnish professional design services unless:

options.A: The contract documents specifically call for such professional services
options.B: The architect requests the services in writing after reviewing submittals
options.C: The delegated portion exceeds a stated dollar threshold in the agreement
options.D: The contractor voluntarily retains a design professional for those services

questions.explanation: A201 does not make the contractor responsible for services amounting to the practice of architecture or engineering. That obligation arises only where the contract documents expressly require such design services for some portion of the work.
questions.source: delegated design under the general conditions

questions.question: Under AIA A201, a Construction Change Directive (G714) is used when:

options.A: The contract has been terminated and the work is being closed out by the surety
options.B: The owner and contractor have not agreed on the proposed change in contract sum or time
options.C: Only a minor change consistent with the documents and without cost/time impact is needed
options.D: The owner, contractor, and architect have already agreed on all terms of the change

questions.explanation: The construction change directive is the tool for moving a change forward when the owner and contractor have not yet settled on its effect on price or time. The contractor must proceed with the directed work even though the adjustment remains unresolved.

questions.question: Approved substitutions made before bid opening are typically incorporated by means of:

options.A: An RFI response
options.B: A change order
options.C: A field order
options.D: An addendum

questions.explanation: Before bids are opened, an addendum is the instrument that folds approved substitutions or additional acceptable products into the procurement documents. The change then becomes part of the contract documents when the agreement is executed.

questions.question: In the three-tier hierarchy of requirements, which level provides broadest provisions?

options.A: Division 01—General Requirements
options.B: General Conditions of the contract
options.C: Supplementary Conditions
options.D: PART 1—GENERAL of individual sections

questions.explanation: The general conditions speak in the broadest terms; Division 01 then refines those provisions for the project; and PART 1—GENERAL of each technical section gets very specific to the work of that section. Breadth decreases as you move down the tiers.

questions.question: Division 01 sections should be written in language broad enough to apply to the work of which divisions?

options.A: Divisions 01 through 33 (the original MasterFormat groups)
options.B: Only the technical divisions that are actually used on the project
options.C: Divisions 02 through 49 (all technical specification divisions)
options.D: Divisions 00 through 14 (procurement through conveying systems)

questions.explanation: Because Division 01 carries the general execution requirements for the whole project, its language must be broad enough to reach every technical section, that is, all of Divisions 02 through 49, so the same requirements need not be repeated.

questions.question: Section 01 33 00 should specify minimum review times to cover at least how many submittal cycles?

options.A: Unlimited resubmittals over the project duration
options.B: Three full resubmittal cycles after the first
options.C: At least the first submittal and one resubmittal
options.D: Only the first submittal, with no resubmittals

questions.explanation: Because submittal turnaround is important to the procurement process, the submittal section should give the A/E a stated minimum review period that covers at least the initial submittal plus one resubmittal.

questions.question: By submitting shop drawings under AIA A201, the contractor represents to the owner and architect that it has:

options.A: Waived its right to claim additional contract time arising from the submittal
options.B: Obtained pre-approval of any product substitutions contained in the submittal
options.C: Reviewed them, verified field measurements, and coordinated them with the work
options.D: Transferred responsibility for the design's adequacy to the architect of record

questions.explanation: Submitting a shop drawing under A201 is itself a representation by the contractor that it has reviewed and approved the submittal, confirmed materials and field dimensions, and coordinated the information with the contract documents.

questions.question: Section 01 22 00—Unit Prices must clearly define which of the following?

options.A: The contractor's allowable overhead-and-profit mark-up on unit-price work
options.B: Who is responsible for measuring the actual unit-price quantities
options.C: The minimum insurance limits the contractor must carry for unit-price work
options.D: The total contract sum to be carried for all unit-price line items combined

questions.explanation: The unit prices section has to make clear who measures the quantities actually placed. If that responsibility falls to the owner or its representative, the section also needs to spell out how that measurement is administered and coordinated.

questions.question: When the contract documents require delegated design, the design professional's submittals must bear:

options.A: The seal and signature of the licensed delegated design professional
options.B: The seal and countersignature of the surety furnishing the performance bond
options.C: The architect-of-record's professional seal accepting design responsibility
options.D: The owner's authorization stamp confirming acceptance of the delegated work

questions.explanation: A201 requires that certifications for delegated design come from a properly licensed design professional, whose signature and seal must appear on the drawings, calculations, specifications, certifications, and shop drawings that the professional prepares.
questions.source: delegated design under the general conditions

questions.question: Under AIA Document A201, when are addenda considered instruments of change?

options.A: Only during the procurement phase
options.B: Before execution of the agreement
options.C: After execution of the agreement
options.D: Before receipt of bids only

questions.explanation: A201 treats an addendum as something issued any time before the agreement is signed, which leaves room to negotiate up to that point. This is broader than the EJCDC approach, which cuts off addenda at bid opening.

questions.question: Products the owner buys and supplies for the contractor to install are most appropriately specified in:

options.A: Section 01 64 00—Owner-Furnished Products
options.B: Section 01 26 00—Contract Modification Procedures
options.C: Section 01 73 00—Execution
options.D: Section 01 23 00—Alternates

questions.explanation: When the owner provides products for the contractor to install, the owner-furnished products section is used to set the administrative rules, covering the items' essential characteristics, coordination, scheduling, and receiving.

questions.question: Which document modifies the fixed, standardized provisions of AIA A201 for a specific project?

options.A: The bid form and bid schedule
options.B: The owner-contractor agreement
options.C: Supplementary conditions
options.D: Division 01 General Requirements

questions.explanation: Supplementary conditions are the device for tailoring the standardized language of the general conditions to a particular project or jurisdiction, and they govern over the general conditions where the two differ.

questions.question: Section 01 29 00 specifies requirements for the contractor's submittal of:

options.A: The schedule of values and payment applications
options.B: Shop drawings, product data, and physical samples
options.C: Closeout submittals, warranties, and required bonds
options.D: Substitution requests and product-option proposals

questions.explanation: The payment procedures section governs how the contractor submits its schedule of values and its applications for payment, including the forms to use, the number of copies, and the timing.

questions.question: Where should provisions applicable only during procurement (e.g., bid security) be stated?

options.A: Supplementary conditions
options.B: Procurement requirements
options.C: The agreement
options.D: Division 01 sections

questions.explanation: Anything that matters only while bidding is underway, such as how to obtain documents, bid security, or the bid opening date, belongs in the procurement requirements rather than in Division 01, which governs the construction phase.

questions.question: Which AIA document is used for minor changes in the work that do not require an adjustment in contract sum or time?

options.A: AIA G701, Change Order, signed by all parties
options.B: AIA G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions
options.C: AIA G612, Owner's Instructions to the architect
options.D: AIA G714, Construction Change Directive

questions.explanation: The Architect's Supplemental Instructions form is the standard vehicle for a minor change that stays within the intent of the documents and alters neither the contract sum nor the time. Because nothing financial or scheduling changes, the owner's signature is not needed.

questions.question: Under AIA A201 and ConsensusDocs 200, what does the cash allowance typically cover?

options.A: All labor, materials, overhead, and the contractor's profit
options.B: Materials and equipment delivered to site, including taxes
options.C: Sitework, demolition, and related earthwork operations only
options.D: Only the contractor's overhead and profit on the item

questions.explanation: Under these standard documents the cash allowance is confined to the materials and equipment delivered to the site, taxes included. The associated labor, handling, installation, overhead, and profit are carried separately within the contract sum.

questions.question: Under the UCC, contracts for the sale of goods must generally be in writing to be enforceable when the price exceeds:
questions.explanation: The UCC's statute of frauds for goods sets the writing threshold at sales of more than $500. To be enforceable, that writing must show a sale was made, be signed by the party being held to it, and state a quantity.

questions.question: In the standard project-manual structure, Division 01 General Requirements applies to:

options.A: Only Divisions 02 through 19 of the specifications
options.B: Only the conditions of the contract for construction
options.C: Only the procurement and contracting documents
options.D: All Divisions 02 through 49 of the specifications

questions.explanation: Division 01 sets the general administrative and procedural requirements that reach across every technical division, that is, all of Divisions 02 through 49, rather than applying to just a subset or to the procurement documents.

questions.question: In the three-tier hierarchy of general requirements, which tier provides the BROADEST provisions?

options.A: Division 01
options.B: AIA A201 General Conditions
options.C: MasterFormat division headers
options.D: Individual technical specification sections

questions.explanation: The general conditions sit at the top of the hierarchy and provide the broadest legal and administrative framework. Division 01 then narrows that to project-specific procedures, and the technical sections supply the most detailed work requirements.

questions.question: Which characteristic is typical of Division 01 but NOT of the conditions of the contract?

options.A: Definitions of the basic contract terms used throughout the documents
options.B: The legal relationships and obligations among the owner, A/E, and contractor
options.C: The rights and remedies of the parties in the event of default or dispute
options.D: Detailed, project-specific administrative and procedural requirements

questions.explanation: The conditions of the contract handle the legal side, that is, definitions, relationships, rights, and remedies. Division 01 instead carries the project-specific procedures and administrative mechanics, such as submittals, meetings, and closeout.

questions.question: A bid option adding scope must be coordinated across the Invitation to Bid, the Bid Form, and which Division 01 section?

options.A: 01 23 00 Alternates
options.B: 01 22 00 Unit Prices
options.C: 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures
options.D: 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures

questions.explanation: A priced option that adds scope is an alternate, so the Division 01 alternates section is where each alternate is described and kept consistent with the matching entries on the invitation and the bid form.

questions.question: Which item is NOT one of the basic components normally found in a properly composed addendum?

options.A: Changes to the procurement and contracting requirements, in sequence
options.B: The addendum number and the date of the addendum
options.C: A liquidated-damages calculation for late completion of the work
options.D: Identification of the project and the name and address of the A/E

questions.explanation: A typical addendum carries its number and date, identifies the project and the A/E, lists who receives it, sets out the changes in order, notes attachments, and is signed. A liquidated-damages calculation is not an addendum component; that subject lives in the agreement and supplementary conditions.

questions.question: In the three-party construction bond relationship, the principal is:

options.A: The owner, who is the obligee
options.B: The surety company on the bond
options.C: The contractor, as principal
options.D: The A/E who designed the work

questions.explanation: In a surety bond the contractor is the principal who promises to perform, the owner is the obligee who is protected, and the surety backs the contractor's obligations to the owner.

questions.question: Which insurance protects an employee injured on the job regardless of fault?

options.A: Commercial general liability
options.B: Professional liability (errors and omissions)
options.C: Workers' compensation
options.D: Builder's risk

questions.explanation: Workers' compensation is the no-fault coverage that pays for an employee's on-the-job injuries without regard to who was at fault, and most jurisdictions require it by statute.

questions.question: Who typically authors the conditions of the contract?

options.A: The architect-of-record, while preparing the technical specifications
options.B: The specifier, by editing the firm's Division 01 master guide specification text
options.C: The owner or owner's attorney, frequently using a form such as AIA A201
options.D: The contractor, at the time of contract award and bond procurement

questions.explanation: The conditions of the contract are a legal instrument, so they are normally prepared by the owner or the owner's attorney, very often by adopting a published standard form such as AIA A201 or an EJCDC document.

questions.question: Which item is typically NOT included in the Invitation to Bid itself?

options.A: Detailed product specifications
options.B: Bid security requirements
options.C: Project name and brief description
options.D: Time and place for bid receipt

questions.explanation: The invitation summarizes key bidding information, such as the project name and description, where and when bids are received, and any bid security required. Detailed product specifications are not part of the invitation; they belong in the technical sections.

questions.question: Alternates listed on the bid form must:

options.A: Always be priced as a deduct from the base bid amount
options.B: Be left blank by any bidder that declines to price them
options.C: Match the alternate numbering and descriptions in Section 01 23 00
options.D: Replace any conflicting language in the Section 00 11 13 invitation

questions.explanation: Each alternate on the bid form must line up with the Division 01 alternates section and the rest of the procurement documents, using the same numbering and descriptions so bidders price the same items the documents define.

questions.question: When narrative text is inserted into an existing specification section by addendum, the addendum should:

options.A: Reissue the entire affected section as a clean revised-page replacement set
options.B: State the revision in the transmittal cover letter instead of the body
options.C: Identify the section, article, and paragraph, then quote the new language
options.D: Reference the revision only by the project-manual page number affected

questions.explanation: To keep changes unambiguous, the addendum should pinpoint the section number, article, and paragraph being revised and then set out exactly the language being added or changed, rather than relying on page numbers or a cover letter.

questions.question: Describing a revision in the addendum text itself, without reissuing pages, is BEST suited for:

options.A: Edits that are issued after the contract is awarded
options.B: Wholesale revisions affecting many full specification sections
options.C: Replacement of several full revised drawing sheets
options.D: Small, surgical edits with clear paragraph references

questions.explanation: The narrative method, writing the change directly into the addendum, works best for small, targeted edits where a short written change with a clear paragraph reference is clearer than reissuing whole pages or sections.

questions.question: An alternate that adds bleacher seating is BEST identified as:

options.A: Option A - Add Bleacher Seating to base scope
options.B: Alternate No. 1 - Bleacher Seating Addition (Add)
options.C: Alternate No. 1 - Bleacher Seating (Deduct only)
options.D: ALT-A and ALT-B carrying no add or deduct direction

questions.explanation: Best practice gives each alternate a clear number and an explicit add-or-deduct direction so its effect on price is unmistakable. Calling it 'Alternate No. 1' and marking it as an Add states both. The current term is 'alternate' rather than 'alternative,' and an unnumbered ALT-A/ALT-B form omits the needed price direction.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, a Substitution for Cause must be submitted:

options.A: Immediately on discovery, before related submittals are prepared
options.B: At any time during construction, whenever the contractor can justify it
options.C: Within 60 days after the Notice to Proceed, the convenience-request window
options.D: Only during the bidding period, as part of procurement-phase review

questions.explanation: A substitution driven by a genuine project condition (a substitution for cause) must be raised as soon as the need is discovered and, in any event, early enough that it does not disrupt preparation and review of the related submittals. The 60-day-after-notice-to-proceed window applies to convenience requests, not cause requests.

questions.question: When separate pricing is added for one specific floor-tile product, the documents to edit include:

options.A: Only Division 01, since pricing procedures live in the general requirements
options.B: The bid form, the Division 01 pricing section, and the affected technical section
options.C: Only Section 09 30 13 Ceramic Tile, since just one specified product is involved here
options.D: Only the general conditions, which govern price and payment for the contract

questions.explanation: Setting up separate pricing for one product touches three places that must agree: the bid form where the price is entered, the Division 01 alternates or unit-prices section that establishes the procedure, and the technical section that specifies the product itself.

questions.question: When an MBE/DBE participation goal is added to a project, the requirements should be located in:

options.A: The general and supplementary conditions plus Division 01 sections
options.B: The bid form alone, where the bidder lists 1 participation percentage
options.C: An informal A/E memorandum issued to bidders during procurement
options.D: Each affected technical section, product by product and trade by trade

questions.explanation: A participation goal of this kind is a contractual and administrative requirement, so it is set in the supplementary conditions together with a Division 01 administrative section, with the bid form used to capture the bidder's documentation. It is not scattered through the technical sections.

questions.question: LEED Gold certification as a project goal would be most directly addressed in which Division 01 Level 2 section?

options.A: 01 10 00 Summary
options.B: 01 81 13 Sustainable Design Requirements
options.C: 01 33 00 Submittal Procedures
options.D: 01 50 00 Temporary Facilities and Controls

questions.explanation: A green-certification goal and the administration of its credits belong in the sustainable design requirements section, 01 81 13, which sits within the performance requirements group of Division 01.

questions.question: Quality control requirements, including mockups and field testing, are best addressed in which Division 01 Level 2 section group?

options.A: 01 40 00 Quality Requirements
options.B: 01 70 00 Execution and Closeout Requirements
options.C: 01 30 00 Administrative Requirements
options.D: 01 45 00 Quality Control and assurance

questions.explanation: Project-wide quality matters, references, mockups, quality control, and testing, are gathered in the 01 40 00 Quality Requirements group of Division 01.

questions.question: Per typical Division 01 RFI procedural rules, a subcontractor is:

options.A: Prohibited from submitting RFIs directly; the A/E returns them unanswered
options.B: Permitted to submit RFIs to the A/E, but only for shop-drawing matters
options.C: Required to route its RFIs to the A/E through the owner's project representative
options.D: Permitted to submit RFIs directly to the A/E, parallel to the prime contractor

questions.explanation: RFIs must move through the prime contractor to preserve the contractual chain of communication. A subcontractor, not being a party to the prime contract, cannot send RFIs straight to the A/E; such RFIs are returned without an answer.

questions.question: An RFI submitted to request a different product than the one specified is:

options.A: Improper; substitution requests must use the Section 01 25 00 procedure
options.B: Permitted, but only after the contract is awarded and the NTP has issued
options.C: The proper procedure, since an RFI seeks 1 interpretation, not a product change
options.D: Permitted, but only during bidding before bids are received by the owner

questions.explanation: An RFI is for interpreting the documents, not for proposing a different product. A request to use another product has to go through the formal substitution procedure in Section 01 25 00.

questions.question: When the A/E receives an incomplete or inaccurately prepared RFI, the A/E is generally:

options.A: Obligated to forward the RFI to the owner, who may then supply the response
options.B: Obligated to fill in the missing information and respond for the contractor
options.C: Not obligated to respond, and can return the RFI to the contractor to complete
options.D: Obligated to respond within the standard time frame in spite of the deficiencies

questions.explanation: The A/E is not required to answer an RFI that is incomplete or inaccurate and may send it back to be corrected. The response time does not begin to run until a proper RFI is received.

questions.question: Per a typical Section 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures, within how many days after receipt of a substitution request must the A/E request additional information needed to complete the review?

options.A: 14 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 7 days
options.D: 21 days

questions.explanation: A common substitution procedure gives the A/E a seven-day window after receiving the request to ask for any further information or documentation needed to evaluate it. The longer periods listed apply to other steps in the process, not to this request for additional data.

questions.question: Per AIA A701 Instructions to Bidders, procurement-phase substitution requests must be submitted no later than:

options.A: At least 30 days before the bid opening
options.B: At least 14 days before the bid opening
options.C: At least 7 days before receipt of bids
options.D: On the day fixed for the bid opening

questions.explanation: The AIA Instructions to Bidders requires that bidder questions and substitution requests reach the A/E at least seven days before bids are received, leaving time to issue any needed addenda before the deadline.

questions.question: When the A/E requests additional information needed to respond to an RFI, the A/E's response time clock typically:

options.A: Continues to run from the original RFI date
options.B: Resets and runs from receipt of the requested additional information
options.C: Is forfeited if the additional information is not provided within 48 hours
options.D: Is suspended only with written owner consent

questions.explanation: If the A/E has to ask for more information before answering an RFI, the response period restarts and is measured from the date that additional information is received, not from the date of the original RFI.

questions.question: Per a typical Section 01 26 13 Request for Information, within how many days after receiving an RFI must the architect respond with the requested information or interpretation?

options.A: 5 days
options.B: 3 days
options.C: 7 days
options.D: 14 days

questions.explanation: A representative RFI procedure has the contractor submit immediately on discovery and gives the architect five days from receipt to respond. The seven-day figure does not apply to either of these steps.

questions.question: Builder's Risk insurance on a construction project typically covers:

options.A: Damage to the work under construction from fire, theft, or weather
options.B: Design errors and omissions committed by the A/E of record
options.C: The contractor's outright failure to complete the whole project
options.D: Liability for bodily injury to third parties who are present on the site

questions.explanation: Builder's risk is a form of property insurance covering physical loss or damage to the work as it is being built, usually including stored materials. It is distinct from liability coverage, performance bonds, and professional liability insurance.

questions.question: On a federal construction project subject to the Davis-Bacon Act, the contractor must:

options.A: Pay laborers and mechanics no less than the locally prevailing wage rates
options.B: Pay every worker the federal minimum wage established under the FLSA
options.C: Restrict hiring to U.S. citizens for all on-site laborers and mechanics
options.D: Employ only union-affiliated labor on all covered classifications of work

questions.explanation: On covered federal projects, the Davis-Bacon Act requires that laborers and mechanics be paid at least the locally prevailing wages and fringe benefits as determined by the U.S. Department of Labor. It is a prevailing-wage rule, not a citizenship or union-membership requirement.

questions.question: Under the UCC, the implied warranty of merchantability means the goods must:

options.A: Be sourced from domestic manufacturers to satisfy Buy-American provisions
options.B: Be accompanied by an express written warranty from the manufacturer of record
options.C: Be offered at the lowest price available for comparable goods in the market
options.D: Be fit for the ordinary purposes for which such goods are customarily used

questions.explanation: When the seller deals in goods of that kind, the UCC implies a warranty of merchantability, meaning the goods must be fit for the ordinary uses to which such goods are put. This differs from the separate implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose.

questions.question: AIA Document G701 (Change Order) requires signatures from:

options.A: The architect and the contractor only
options.B: The owner, architect, and contractor
options.C: The owner and the contractor only
options.D: The owner and the bonding surety only

questions.explanation: Because a change order records mutual agreement on a scope change and its cost and time effects, the AIA change order form is signed by all three parties: owner, architect, and contractor.

questions.question: An owner asks the A/E whether a critical scope change may be issued after bids are opened but before the contract is signed. Under AIA Document A201, addenda may be issued up until:

options.A: Receipt of bids, after which only change orders may modify the contract documents
options.B: Substantial completion, provided the contractor consents in writing
options.C: The end of the bidding period fixed in the Invitation to Bid notice
options.D: Execution of the agreement, per the private owner's freedom to negotiate

questions.explanation: A201 lets addenda be issued any time before the agreement is executed, which reflects a private owner's freedom to keep negotiating up to signing. The EJCDC approach is stricter, ending addenda at the receipt of bids.

questions.question: On a public works project governed by EJCDC C-700, the latest point at which an addendum may be issued is:

options.A: Receipt of bids, per public-works limits on post-opening changes
options.B: The pre-bid conference, after which the procurement documents freeze
options.C: Award of the contract to the lowest responsive bidder
options.D: Execution of the owner-contractor agreement

questions.explanation: Under the EJCDC public-works model an addendum is a pre-bid instrument, so the last point to issue one is the receipt of bids. Public procurement policy generally forbids changing the documents after opening but before execution. The AIA's later cutoff reflects the private-owner view.

questions.question: A bidder submits a written question nine days before bid opening on a project using AIA A701 Instructions to Bidders. The A/E should treat the question as:

options.A: Timely only if accompanied by a formal substitution request form
options.B: Timely, because A701 requires questions 7 days before receipt of bids
options.C: Untimely, because A701 requires questions 10 days before opening
options.D: Untimely, because questions may be raised only at the pre-bid meeting

questions.explanation: The AIA Instructions to Bidders sets a minimum of seven days before bids are received for questions and substitution requests, so a question submitted nine days out is within the window and timely. The ten-day figure comes from the EJCDC recommendation, not A701.

questions.question: A minor addendum that does not change cost or time can ordinarily be issued without imposing hardship on bidders as late as:

options.A: The morning of bid opening
options.B: Four days before the bid or proposal due date
options.C: Ten days before the bid or proposal due date
options.D: Seven days before the bid or proposal due date

questions.explanation: A small addendum with no cost or time impact can sometimes be issued as late as roughly four days before the due date without unfairly burdening bidders. A significant last-minute change, by contrast, should prompt advising the owner and, if possible, postponing the bid date.

questions.question: Where individual prime contracts are awarded on one project, addenda should be numbered:

options.A: Only by date, omitting sequential numbers to avoid confusion
options.B: By affected specification section number rather than sequentially
options.C: In a separate consecutive series for each prime contract
options.D: In a single continuous series shared across all the contracts

questions.explanation: Addenda are numbered consecutively, but when a project is let as several separate prime contracts, each contract gets its own consecutive series of addenda numbers to keep the changes for each contract clear.

questions.question: Procurement documents are obtained at the A/E's office upon a $100 deposit per set. A firm that obtains documents but does not submit a bid, then returns them in good condition, is typically entitled to:

options.A: The full $100 deposit, identical to a returning bidder
options.B: A partial refund of $75, less than a returning bidder receives
options.C: A credit toward documents on the owner's next advertised project
options.D: No refund, because only actual bidders may recover the deposit

questions.explanation: It is common for a bidder that returns documents in good condition after bid opening to recover the full deposit, while a non-bidder that returns documents recovers only a reduced amount. With a $100 deposit, that reduced refund here is $75.

questions.question: Procurement documents may typically be examined by interested parties:

options.A: Only at the office of the lowest responsible bidder of record
options.B: At the construction site trailer once the contract is awarded
options.C: Only by appointment at the owner's purchasing department
options.D: At the A/E's office and at named plan rooms or plan centers

questions.explanation: Interested parties can usually examine the procurement documents at the A/E's office and at designated plan rooms or plan centers. Examining the documents is separate from obtaining a deposited set to bid from.

questions.question: The Instructions to Bidders should explain that issuing partial copies of the documents is:

options.A: Required for subcontractors who bid only a single trade
options.B: Permitted only for the mechanical and electrical divisions
options.C: Encouraged, in order to reduce the owner's reproduction cost
options.D: To be avoided, because incomplete sets cause bidding errors

questions.explanation: The Instructions to Bidders should address how documents are made available and caution that partial sets should be avoided, since bidding from an incomplete set invites errors. They also cover the conditions, timing, and refunds for returning documents.

questions.question: A public agency receives a sealed bid a few minutes past the bid-opening deadline fixed in the Invitation to Bid. The agency should:

options.A: Refuse it, because bids received past the established time are not accepted
options.B: Hold it unopened until the next regularly scheduled public agency board meeting
options.C: Accept it if apparent low, since the public benefits from lower pricing
options.D: Accept it if the envelope was postmarked before the stated deadline date

questions.explanation: On public work, bids must arrive before the established opening time. A bid received even slightly late is not accepted, regardless of how low it may appear, in order to preserve the fairness of the public bidding process.

questions.question: When all bids for a public contract exceed the established budget, the bids are rejected and the customary remedies are to:

options.A: Award to the low bidder and absorb the overage as a contingency
options.B: Negotiate privately with the three lowest bidders to cut scope
options.C: Re-advertise at once with the same documents and a longer period
options.D: Increase funding, redesign through value analysis, or abandon it

questions.explanation: If every bid comes in over budget, the bids are rejected and the security and deposits returned. The owner's usual options are to add funding, redesign the project through value analysis to lower cost, or abandon it.

questions.question: Public bids are required to be sealed in an opaque envelope, signed by an authorized signatory, complete with all supplements, and:

options.A: Accompanied by the contractor's audited financial statements
options.B: Submitted prior to the established time for bid opening
options.C: Notarized by a commissioned notary before submission
options.D: Delivered in person by an officer of the bidding firm

questions.explanation: A conforming public bid must be complete, signed by someone authorized to bind the bidder, sealed in an opaque envelope as the instructions require, and delivered before the established opening time. Timeliness is the missing requirement here.

questions.question: Which item is NOT a standard component of a properly composed addendum?

options.A: The changes to the procurement and contracting requirements, in sequence
options.B: A statement of the contractor's anticipated overhead and profit markup
options.C: The addendum number and date
options.D: Identification of the project and the A/E's name and address

questions.explanation: A properly composed addendum carries its number and date, identifies the project and the A/E, names the recipients, lists the changes in sequence, notes attachments, and is signed. A statement of the contractor's overhead and profit is a change-order pricing matter, not part of an addendum.

questions.question: A specifier must locate a provision establishing the legal relationships, rights, and remedies among the owner, contractor, and A/E. This belongs in:

options.A: The conditions of the contract, such as AIA A201, not Division 01
options.B: Each affected technical section under its own Part 1 General article
options.C: Division 01 General Requirements, Section 01 10 00 Summary
options.D: The Invitation to Bid issued during the procurement phase

questions.explanation: Legal relationships, rights, and remedies among the parties are the province of the conditions of the contract, such as AIA A201. Division 01 instead carries project-specific administrative and procedural requirements, not the legal framework.

questions.question: In the three-tier hierarchy of general administrative and procedural requirements, which sequence runs from BROADEST to most specific?

options.A: Conditions of the contract, Division 01, technical sections
options.B: Technical sections, Division 01, conditions of the contract
options.C: Conditions of the contract, technical sections, Division 01
options.D: Division 01, conditions of the contract, technical sections

questions.explanation: Breadth runs from the conditions of the contract, which set the broadest framework, down through Division 01, which adapts those provisions across all divisions, to the technical sections, which give the most specific work requirements.

questions.question: A requirement governing the contractor's schedule of values and applications for funds is most properly placed in:

options.A: Section 01 29 00 Payment Procedures
options.B: Section 01 26 00 Contract Modification Procedures
options.C: The agreement between the owner and contractor
options.D: Section 01 22 00 Unit Prices

questions.explanation: The payment procedures section is the home for requirements on the schedule of values and the applications for payment, including the forms, copies, and timing involved.

questions.question: The Instructions to Bidders are the proper place to tell a bidder how to identify and submit the completed bid, including:

options.A: The detailed technical product specifications that each bidder must satisfy in order to be deemed responsive
options.B: The schedule of values the contractor will use for applications for payment
options.C: The penal sum of the performance and payment bonds the successful bidder must furnish
options.D: The project and contract number, owner, bid date and time, bidder name, and sealed-envelope requirement

questions.explanation: The Instructions to Bidders cover how to identify and submit the bid, the project and contract number, the owner, the bid date and time, the bidder's name, and the sealed-envelope requirement, along with bid preparation, bid security, and how to modify or withdraw a bid. Product specifications, bond penal sums, and the schedule of values are dealt with elsewhere.

questions.question: Which characteristic is typical of Division 01 but NOT of the conditions of the contract?

options.A: The rights and remedies of the parties upon default or dispute
options.B: The legal obligations among the owner, A/E, and contractor
options.C: Detailed, project-specific administrative and procedural rules
options.D: Definitions of basic contract terms used throughout the documents

questions.explanation: The conditions of the contract supply definitions, legal relationships, and rights and remedies. Division 01 is where the detailed, project-specific procedures live, covering submittals, meetings, quality, and closeout.

questions.question: Who typically prepares the conditions of the contract for a project?

options.A: The contractor, at the time of bond and insurance procurement
options.B: The specifier, by editing the firm's Division 01 master guide
options.C: The owner or owner's attorney, commonly adopting A201 or C-700
options.D: The architect-of-record, as part of the technical specifications

questions.explanation: Being a legal document, the conditions of the contract are normally prepared by the owner or the owner's attorney, frequently by adopting a published standard form such as AIA A201 or an EJCDC document.

questions.question: A project sets a LEED Gold goal. The credit administration, documentation, and certification submittals are most directly specified in:

options.A: Section 01 45 00 Quality Control
options.B: Section 01 33 00 Submittal Procedures
options.C: Section 01 91 13 General Commissioning Requirements
options.D: Section 01 81 13 Sustainable Design Requirements

questions.explanation: Green-certification goals and the administration of their credits are specified in the sustainable design requirements section, 01 81 13, which falls within the performance requirements group of Division 01.

questions.question: General requirements for the start-up acceptance process, including the agent's role, are specified in Division 01 under:

options.A: Section 01 94 00 Facility Decommissioning
options.B: Section 01 91 00 Commissioning
options.C: Section 01 79 00 Demonstration and Training
options.D: Section 01 77 00 Closeout Procedures

questions.explanation: Commissioning the facility, the role of the commissioning agent, and coordination of the commissioning process are specified in the commissioning section, 01 91 00 (with its general commissioning requirements). Decommissioning, by contrast, is covered in 01 94 00.

questions.question: Per CSI SectionFormat, an Action Submittal differs from an Informational Submittal in that it:

options.A: Requires responsive review by the A/E, while an informational one does not
options.B: Is submitted at closeout, while an informational one is submitted during work
options.C: Is reviewed by the owner, while an informational one is reviewed by the A/E
options.D: Is required only on public projects, while an informational one is optional

questions.explanation: An action submittal, such as product data, a shop drawing, or a sample, is one the A/E must act on by reviewing and responding. An informational submittal is provided for the record and does not call for that responsive action. Both categories are defined in Division 01.

questions.question: An owner adds an MBE/DBE participation goal during procurement. The requirements are best located in:

options.A: Each affected technical section, organized trade by trade
options.B: The bid form alone, where each bidder lists its participation percentage
options.C: An informal A/E memorandum issued to the bidders during the 1 procurement phase
options.D: The supplementary conditions plus a Division 01 section, with bid-form support

questions.explanation: A participation goal is addressed in the supplementary conditions and a Division 01 administrative section, with the bid form capturing the bidder's documentation. It is not spread across the technical sections.

questions.question: End-of-service-life shutdown requirements for a building are specified in:

options.A: Section 01 77 00 Closeout Procedures
options.B: Section 01 91 00 Commissioning of the facility
options.C: Section 01 94 00 Facility Decommissioning
options.D: Section 01 78 00 Closeout Submittals and records

questions.explanation: Activities for taking a facility out of service at the end of its life are specified in the facility decommissioning section, 01 94 00, which is distinct from commissioning and from the project closeout sections.

questions.question: A specifier must place general requirements and procedures for the team's value-analysis process. The correct Division 01 section is:

options.A: Section 01 22 00 Unit Prices
options.B: Section 01 24 00 Value Analysis
options.C: Section 01 21 00 Allowances
options.D: Section 01 23 00 Alternates list

questions.explanation: The general requirements and procedures for value analysis are set in the value analysis section, 01 24 00.

questions.question: An item whose exact quantity is unknown at bid time but whose rate can be fixed, paid as installed, is best handled as a:

options.A: Cash allowance under Section 01 21 13
options.B: Alternate under Section 01 23 00
options.C: Measured price under Section 01 22 00
options.D: Quantity allowance under Section 01 21 19

questions.explanation: When the quantity of an item is uncertain at bid time but a price per unit can be agreed, a unit price (Section 01 22 00) is the right device: the installed quantity is measured and paid at that agreed rate. A cash allowance instead fixes a dollar sum for a deferred selection.

questions.question: An owner wants a defined scope item priced separately so it can be accepted or declined at award. This is specified as a(n):

options.A: Unit price in Section 01 22 00
options.B: Alternate in Section 01 23 00
options.C: Contract modification in Section 01 26 00
options.D: Allowance in Section 01 21 00

questions.explanation: A defined scope item that the owner can take or leave at award, priced separately on the bid form, is an alternate (Section 01 23 00). Each affected technical section then cross-references that alternates section.

questions.question: A dollar sum is carried in the contract for finish hardware whose specific product the owner has not yet selected, to be reconciled against actual cost. This device is a:

options.A: Cash allowance under Section 01 21 13
options.B: Deduct alternate under Section 01 23 00
options.C: Quantity allowance under Section 01 21 19
options.D: Unit price under Section 01 22 00

questions.explanation: Carrying a stated dollar sum for a product whose selection is deferred, then reconciling it against the actual cost by change order, is a cash allowance (Section 01 21 13). A quantity allowance instead fixes an estimated quantity of installed work.

questions.question: Each specification section affected by an alternate should:

options.A: Restate the full alternate text to avoid cross-refs
options.B: Be omitted from the base bid until 1 is accepted
options.C: Carry its own independent alternate number
options.D: Cross-reference Section 01 23 00 Alternates

questions.explanation: Alternates are described once in the alternates section, and each affected technical section simply cross-references that section rather than restating the alternate. Not every alternate is product-based, so this keeps the documents consistent.

questions.question: To add separate pricing for one specific floor-tile product on a competitively bid project, the documents that must be coordinated are:

options.A: Only Division 01, since pricing lives within the general requirements
options.B: Only the general conditions, which govern price and payment of the work
options.C: Only the affected technical section, since one specified product changes
options.D: The bid form, the Division 01 pricing section, and the technical section

questions.explanation: Separate pricing for a product requires three documents to agree: the bid form, the Division 01 alternates or unit-prices section establishing the procedure, and the technical section that specifies the product.

questions.question: When the installed quantity of an item carried as a quantity allowance differs from the estimate in Section 01 21 19, the difference is reconciled by:

options.A: Carrying the variance to closeout as a punch-list credit item
options.B: Absorbing the variance entirely within the contractor's overhead and profit
options.C: A change order adjusting the contract sum for the measured over/under-run
options.D: Re-bidding the affected scope as a deduct alternate to the contract sum

questions.explanation: A quantity allowance fixes an estimated quantity of installed work. When the measured quantity differs, the contract sum is adjusted by change order at the established rate for the over-run or under-run, much like unit-price reconciliation.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, after receiving a substitution request the architect will request any additional information or documentation needed for evaluation within:

options.A: 48 hours of receipt of the request
options.B: 15 days of receipt of the request
options.C: 30 days of receipt of the request
options.D: 7 days of receipt of the request

questions.explanation: A common substitution procedure gives the architect seven days from receipt of the request to ask for any further information needed to evaluate it. The fifteen-day figure is instead the window for notifying the contractor whether the substitution is accepted or rejected.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, the architect will notify the contractor of the decision to accept or reject a proposed substitution within:

options.A: 15 days of receipt of the request
options.B: 10 days of receipt of the request
options.C: 7 days of receipt of the request
options.D: 20 days of receipt of the request

questions.explanation: A representative substitution procedure has the architect notify the contractor of acceptance or rejection within fifteen days of receiving the request. The seven-day period applies only to asking for additional information, not to the decision.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, a Substitution for Cause must be submitted immediately on discovery of the need for change, but no later than:

options.A: 15 days after the related submittal package is logged
options.B: 20 days prior to the time required for preparation and review of related submittals
options.C: 60 days after the Notice to Proceed
options.D: 7 days before the related submittal is logged, reviewed, and returned by the architect

questions.explanation: A substitution for cause is raised as soon as the need is discovered and, in any event, far enough ahead, on the order of twenty days, that it does not interfere with preparation and review of the related submittals. The sixty-day-after-notice-to-proceed limit applies to convenience requests.

questions.question: In a typical Section 01 25 00, the architect will consider a Substitution for Convenience only if the request is received:

options.A: At any time during construction if it benefits the owner
options.B: Within 20 days prior to preparation of related submittals
options.C: Within 7 days of the Notice to Proceed
options.D: Within 60 days after the Notice to Proceed

questions.explanation: A convenience substitution, one offered for advantage rather than necessity, is considered only when the request comes in within sixty days after the notice to proceed. The twenty-day rule governs substitutions for cause instead.

questions.question: A contractor's substitution request that is incomplete or does not comply with Section 01 25 00 will typically be:

options.A: Forwarded to the owner for a discretionary waiver
options.B: Logged as approved-as-noted pending a resubmittal
options.C: Held by the architect until the 15-day clock expires, then approved by default
options.D: Returned without action, except to record noncompliance

questions.explanation: A substitution request that is incomplete or fails to follow the section's requirements is returned without action, except to note the noncompliance. There is no approval by default if the architect simply lets time pass.

questions.question: During the procurement (bidding/negotiating) phase, the standardized CSI substitution request form is:

options.A: AIA Document G701, the change order form
options.B: CSI Form 1.5C, the pre-award substitution request
options.C: CSI Form 13.1A, the post-award substitution request
options.D: CSI Form 13.2A, the request for information

questions.explanation: CSI provides a substitution request form for use during the bidding and negotiating phase, Form 1.5C. A different CSI form, 13.1A, is used after that phase once the project is under construction.

questions.question: A construction-phase substitution request on a typical Section 01 25 00 project should use:

options.A: CSI Form 1.5C, the bidding-phase substitution request
options.B: CSI Form 13.2A, the request for information
options.C: AIA Document G710, Architect's Supplemental Instructions
options.D: CSI Form 13.1A, the post-bid substitution request

questions.explanation: Once construction is under way, substitution requests use the post-bid CSI form, 13.1A. Form 1.5C is the bidding-phase substitution form, and 13.2A is the RFI form.

questions.question: A contractor proposes a tile by a different manufacturer instead of the specified product, citing only a cost saving and no project condition. This is a:

options.A: Comparable product submittal, requiring no substitution review
options.B: Minor change in the work, by architect's supplemental instructions
options.C: Substitution for Cause, because a different product is involved here
options.D: Substitution for Convenience, offering advantage but not required

questions.explanation: A change that the project does not require but that the contractor offers for an advantage like cost is a substitution for convenience, which is considered only if requested within the sixty-day window after the notice to proceed.

questions.question: A contractor must replace a specified product that can no longer satisfy a newly amended building-code requirement. This is a:

options.A: Substitution for Convenience, governed by the 60-day NTP window
options.B: Comparable product submittal under the product requirements section
options.C: Substitution for Cause, since the amended code compels the change
options.D: Request for information, since it raises a code-interpretation question

questions.explanation: A change forced by a project condition, such as an amended code the specified product can no longer meet, is a substitution for cause. It must be raised promptly and ahead of the related submittals, not within the convenience window.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the owner and contractor have not agreed on the cost and time impact of a directed change, but the work must proceed now. The proper instrument is the:

options.A: Construction change directive (AIA G714)
options.B: Architect's supplemental instructions (AIA G710)
options.C: Change order (AIA G701)
options.D: Minor change in the work

questions.explanation: A construction change directive is the instrument for ordering a change to begin before the parties have agreed on its effect on contract sum or time. A change order requires that prior agreement, and a minor change carries no cost or time impact at all.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, a construction change directive is prepared by the architect and signed by:

options.A: The owner, architect, and contractor
options.B: The owner and contractor only
options.C: The owner and architect
options.D: The architect only

questions.explanation: Because a construction change directive orders work before the contractor has agreed to the adjustment, it is prepared by the architect and signed by the owner and architect. A change order, by contrast, carries all three signatures.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, which document requires the signatures of the owner, contractor, AND architect?

options.A: AIA G704 Certificate of Substantial Completion
options.B: AIA G701 Change Order
options.C: AIA G714 Construction Change Directive
options.D: AIA G710 Architect's Supplemental Instructions

questions.explanation: The change order is prepared by the architect and signed by the owner, contractor, and architect, recording their agreement on the change and on the related adjustments to sum and time.

questions.question: An architect directs the contractor to make a clarifying change that involves no adjustment to contract sum or time. Under AIA A201, the architect may issue this as a minor change because:

options.A: It must be priced by the contractor before it becomes binding
options.B: The owner's countersignature converts it into a change order
options.C: It does not require the owner's signature and is within the architect's authority
options.D: The contractor may decline to perform it until a priced change order has been negotiated

questions.explanation: A201 gives the architect authority to order minor changes that are consistent with the documents' intent and affect neither sum nor time. Such a change, issued in writing, is binding without the owner's signature.

questions.question: Under EJCDC C-700, the instrument that orders a change before agreement on price or time, signed only by the owner, is the:

options.A: Field order issued with no standard form
options.B: Work change directive, EJCDC C-940 form
options.C: Written amendment to the agreement terms
options.D: Change order, the EJCDC C-941 form

questions.explanation: In the EJCDC system the work change directive is signed by the owner and directs additions, deletions, or revisions before the effect on price or time is settled. The EJCDC change order, by contrast, is signed by the engineer, owner, and contractor.

questions.question: Under AIA A201, the contract sum or contract time can be adjusted ONLY by:

options.A: A directive in the meeting minutes acknowledged by the contractor
options.B: A written change order
options.C: A field order issued by the architect
options.D: Architect's supplemental instructions

questions.explanation: Under A201 the only instrument that actually adjusts the contract sum or time is a written change order. A construction change directive can start the work before agreement, but the adjustment itself is later recorded by change order.

questions.question: The distinguishing factor that separates a purchasing (goods) contract from a construction contract is that the goods contractor:

options.A: Is involved in little or no on-site activity such as construction or installation
options.B: Always provides a performance bond, while the construction contractor does not
options.C: Is selected by negotiation, while the construction contractor is competitively bid
options.D: Is governed by AIA A201 rather than by the Uniform Commercial Code

questions.explanation: What sets a goods contract apart is that the supplier performs little or no work at the site. If the supplier must take part in installation, the arrangement becomes a furnish-and-install subcontract rather than a pure purchasing contract.

questions.question: Under the Uniform Commercial Code, mercantile terms such as FOB (free on board) and CIF establish responsibility for:

options.A: The buyer's right to reject nonconforming goods
options.B: Transportation costs, insurance, and risk of loss
options.C: The quantity term that must be stated for enforceability
options.D: The seller's implied warranty of merchantability only

questions.explanation: Shipping terms like FOB and CIF allocate transportation costs, insurance, and the risk of loss between buyer and seller. Absent such terms, the UCC assigns risk of loss based on how far performance has progressed.

questions.question: Under UCC Article 2, a written contract for the sale of goods is enforceable if it provides evidence of a sale, is signed by the party to be charged, and:

options.A: Includes an express warranty of fitness
options.B: States a delivery date certain
options.C: Specifies a quantity
options.D: Recites the agreed unit price

questions.explanation: For a goods contract to satisfy the UCC writing requirement it must evidence a sale, bear the signature of the party to be held to it, and state a quantity. The UCC can fill in a missing price or delivery term, but quantity generally has to be agreed.

questions.question: Under the UCC, contracts for the sale of goods must be in writing to be enforceable when the goods cost more than:
questions.explanation: The UCC's statute of frauds for goods requires a writing once the sale exceeds $500. The $2,000 figure is the trigger for the federal Davis-Bacon prevailing-wage rule, a different matter entirely.

questions.question: In the EJCDC procurement documents, the party that furnishes the goods is referred to as the Seller and the owner is referred to as the:

options.A: Principal
options.B: Constructor
options.C: Obligee
options.D: Buyer

questions.explanation: EJCDC procurement documents use sale terminology: the supplier of the goods is the Seller and the owner is the Buyer. Principal and obligee are bond terms, not purchasing terms.

questions.question: Which EJCDC procurement document is the Agreement Between Buyer and Seller for Procurement?

options.A: EJCDC P-700
options.B: EJCDC P-520
options.C: EJCDC P-200
options.D: EJCDC P-400

questions.explanation: Among the core EJCDC procurement documents, the agreement between buyer and seller is P-520. The others in the set are the instructions to bidders, the general conditions, and the bid form.

questions.question: The EJCDC procurement (purchasing) documents are NOT intended for use where:

options.A: The goods are competitively bid using a standard goods bid form
options.B: The manufacturer or supplier must participate in on-site installation
options.C: Multiple deliveries of the same engineered item are anticipated
options.D: The owner purchases engineered materials directly from the goods provider

questions.explanation: The purchasing documents are not meant for situations where the supplier must take part in installation. That looks more like a construction contract, so construction forms, or purchasing documents modified for the purpose, should be used instead.

questions.question: Depending on the goods and their disposition, the bond usually required on a purchasing contract is a performance bond because it:

options.A: Protects the goods contractor's sub-suppliers and fabricators against non-payment for materials
options.B: Guarantees the buyer will accept and pay for the goods on delivery
options.C: Replaces the need for property insurance on goods at the site
options.D: Provides the owner recourse for non-performance in manufacture, supply, or delivery

questions.explanation: On a purchasing contract a performance bond gives the owner recourse if the supplier fails to manufacture, supply, or deliver the goods as agreed. That is different from a payment bond or from property insurance.

questions.question: One valid reason an owner may purchase major equipment under a separate purchasing contract in advance of construction is to:

options.A: Avoid having to coordinate the purchasing and construction documents
options.B: Gain lead time on goods requiring long fabrication periods and avoid construction delays
options.C: Transfer all risk of late or incomplete delivery to the construction contractor at no owner cost
options.D: Eliminate the need for submittals on the purchased goods

questions.explanation: Buying long-lead equipment early can secure fabrication time, lock in budget, hedge against shortages, and capture tax advantages. It does not simplify coordination; in fact, managing two sets of documents becomes more demanding, not less.

questions.question: The AIA standard form used for purchasing goods, which references the UCC, is:

options.A: AIA A101, the standard stipulated-sum agreement between owner and construction contractor
options.B: AIA A152 Purchase Order, with its companion A152 Exhibit A Terms and Conditions
options.C: AIA A312 Performance and Payment Bond
options.D: AIA A701 Instructions to Bidders

questions.explanation: The AIA purchase order form (A152, with its Exhibit A terms and conditions) is used for buying goods and references the UCC, though it does not declare that its own terms prevail in a conflict.

questions.question: When an owner buys goods under a purchasing contract for the construction contractor to install, a foreseeable risk the documents must address is that:

options.A: The construction contractor may not warrant goods it did not supply
options.B: The goods contractor may carry builder's risk for the whole project
options.C: The owner is relieved of responsibility for delivery time and storage
options.D: The UCC may not apply to the purchase because installation is involved
