Of three offered units - (A) 1/4-in annealed; (B) insulated unit with a laminated outboard and a 1/4-in annealed clear lite; (C) insulating unit of a 1/4-in annealed lite and a 1/4-in heat-strengthened lite - how many units satisfy the safety-glass inboard-lite requirement?

options.A: None of the units, because skylights require fully tempered glass on both lites
options.B: Exactly two units, because heat-strengthened glass would also count as safety glazing here
options.C: All three units, because any insulated glass unit qualifies as safety glazing
options.D: Exactly one unit, because only the laminated-glass unit qualifies as safety glazing

questions.explanation: Among the three units, only the one using laminated glass qualifies as safety glazing for the inboard lite. Annealed and heat-strengthened glass do not count as safety glazing, so exactly one unit meets the requirement.

questions.question: In a heat-island analysis, steep-sloped roofs require a minimum 0.39 initial Solar Reflectance Index (SRI) or 0.32 three-year aged SRI. A steep-sloped (6:12) standing-seam roof reports an initial SRI of 0.82. Against the steep-sloped criteria, that product is:

options.A: Unacceptable, because steep roofs must instead meet the 0.82 low-sloped initial value
options.B: Acceptable only after the AHJ approves the roof's three-year aged SRI value
options.C: Unacceptable, because SRI cannot be applied to metal standing-seam roofing
options.D: Acceptable, because its 0.82 initial SRI exceeds the 0.39 steep-sloped minimum

questions.explanation: Steep-sloped roofs need at least a 0.39 initial SRI (or 0.32 aged). An initial SRI of 0.82 clears the 0.39 steep-sloped threshold, so the roof is acceptable; steep roofs are not held to the higher low-sloped value.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a GENERIC product type that must be identified before specific products are researched?

options.A: 8-inch ductile iron pipe, pressure class 150, with restrained push-on joints
options.B: Ductile iron pipe complying with ANSI/AWWA C150/A21.50 and C151/A21.51
options.C: Cement-lined ductile iron pipe with an exterior asphaltic protective coating
options.D: Ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main, before any detailed selection

questions.explanation: The generic description names only the product class and use — ductile iron pipe for a sewer force main — and must be settled before detailed selection. The other choices add size, pressure class, coatings, linings, joint type, and standard designations, which makes them specific rather than generic.

questions.question: The specific-product example for ductile iron pipe cites two ANSI/AWWA designations. Which pair correctly matches the example?

options.A: ASTM A21.50 and ASTM A21.51 for ductile-iron pipe and its fittings
options.B: ANSI A117.1 and ANSI/AWI 0641 for the pipe's thickness and joints
options.C: ASCE/SEI 7 and ACI 350 for the pipe's loads and liquid containment
options.D: ANSI/AWWA C150/A21.50 and ANSI/AWWA C151/A21.51 for the pipe

questions.explanation: The ductile iron pipe example is identified by the designations ANSI/AWWA C150/A21.50 and ANSI/AWWA C151/A21.51. The other pairs substitute real but unrelated designations for accessibility, woodwork, structural loads, or concrete.

questions.question: A manufacturer's website lists both an Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) and a Health Product Declaration (HPD) for a product. These are distinguished in that the:

options.A: EPD and HPD are identical documents issued under two interchangeable names
options.B: EPD instead discloses the products ingredient health hazards, while the HPD reports its life-cycle carbon impacts
options.C: EPD reports the product's environmental life-cycle impacts; the HPD discloses its contents and health hazards
options.D: EPD is issued by the AHJ, while the HPD is issued by the project's design team

questions.explanation: Both documents commonly appear on manufacturer sites but cover different ground. An EPD summarizes a product's environmental and life-cycle impacts, while an HPD discloses its contents and associated health information. They are distinct documents, not AHJ- or designer-issued.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the document types typically available on a manufacturer's website?

options.A: Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) together with the products written installation instructions
options.B: Evaluation service reports and the product's published test reports
options.C: The authority having jurisdiction's signed building permit for the project
options.D: Building information model (BIM) objects and drawing-detail files

questions.explanation: Manufacturer sites typically offer catalogs, datasheets, installation instructions, SDSs, EPDs, HPDs, test and evaluation reports, BIM objects and details, guide specs, representative contacts, and continuing-education materials. A signed project building permit comes from the AHJ, not the manufacturer's website.

questions.question: A normally voluntary reference standard can become MANDATORY on a project when it is:

options.A: Listed in a manufacturer's guide specification for the chosen product
options.B: Maintained in the A/E's current office library of reference standards
options.C: Published by an ANSI-accredited standards-developing organization
options.D: Cited within an adopted code, so that portion becomes codified

questions.explanation: A reference standard is voluntary on its own, but once an adopted code cites it, that referenced portion becomes part of the code's mandatory requirements. Appearing in a guide spec or office library, or being published by an accredited body, does not make a standard mandatory.

questions.question: Codes represent the MINIMUM requirements for a project. Accordingly, the design team:

options.A: Is free to include requirements more stringent than the minimum code requires
options.B: Is barred from specifying requirements stricter than the adopted code allows
options.C: May only meet, but never exceed, the published minimum code requirements
options.D: It must request AHJ permission before exceeding any one of the minimum code requirements

questions.explanation: Because codes set only minimums, they place no ceiling on the design. The team is free to write requirements that are more stringent than the code's minimums, and doing so does not require AHJ permission.

questions.question: Stating 'as required by code' in a specification is INADEQUATE because the specifier should instead:

options.A: Reference only the model-code title and let the contractor research the value
options.B: Defer the requirement to the AHJ to set during the building permit review
options.C: Identify the specific requirement, such as a particular R-value rather than a citation
options.D: Direct the manufacturer to certify whatever R-value the installed product happens to achieve

questions.explanation: 'As required by code' leaves the actual requirement unstated. The specifier should spell out the specific value — for insulation, a particular R-value — rather than just pointing at the code and leaving others to look it up.

questions.question: When more than one code edition could apply, the PREVAILING code for a project is the one that:

options.A: Has jurisdiction over the geographic location of the project
options.B: Is the most recent edition published by the model code-writing body
options.C: Is preferred by the product representative supporting the assembly
options.D: Imposes the least restrictive requirements on the proposed design

questions.explanation: When editions could conflict, the controlling code is the one with jurisdiction over where the project is located. It is not simply the newest edition, the representative's preference, or whichever is least restrictive.

questions.question: A good product representative serving as a 'trusted advisor' is valuable largely because such representatives:

options.A: Replace the A/E's obligation to perform independent product research
options.B: Limit their advice strictly to listing their own product in the specification
options.C: Know their competition's products and help assess benefits and shortcomings
options.D: Hold authority to approve code modifications on the AHJ's behalf

questions.explanation: A representative who acts as a trusted advisor understands competing products as well as their own and can help weigh the strengths and weaknesses of each based on evidence. Consulting one is valuable but does not relieve the A/E of doing independent research.

questions.question: A design team selects a costlier thermal insulation for a building the owner will keep 10 years, justifying it because the better-insulated envelope:

options.A: Eliminates the need for any HVAC equipment in the conditioned spaces
options.B: Lowers the product's first cost below that of the competing insulations
options.C: It is mandated outright by the energy codes minimum prescriptive R-value table for walls
options.D: Allows a smaller HVAC unit and notable operating savings over the period

questions.explanation: The pricier insulation improves the envelope enough to permit a smaller, less costly HVAC unit and to deliver meaningful operating savings across the 10-year ownership. That is a life-cycle justification, not a first-cost one.

questions.question: When a design team is told simply to select the 'best' product, the guidance is that 'best' must be judged by:

options.A: The product with the single highest durability rating available
options.B: The priorities the owner has established for the project
options.C: The lowest first cost among the otherwise comparable products
options.D: The option the product representative recommends most strongly

questions.explanation: 'Best' is not a fixed quality — it can mean most durable, most available, or most economical depending on the situation. The team should define it according to the priorities the owner has set, rather than defaulting to durability, price, or a representative's recommendation.

questions.question: In a hurricane scenario (a 12-story Florida east-coast condo in a High Velocity Wind Zone with an exposed parking deck), the design team should use which material for exposed railings and components?

options.A: Galvanized steel, because its coating fully resists the salt-air exposure
options.B: Aluminum, because it better resists the corrosive coastal salt environment
options.C: Untreated carbon steel, because it is the most economical exposed material
options.D: Any material, because exposure has no bearing in a High Velocity Wind Zone

questions.explanation: On an exposed coastal deck subject to salt air, aluminum holds up better against corrosion than galvanized steel, so it is the preferred material for exposed railings and components.

questions.question: When an A/E meets with an AHJ to request a code modification or interpretation, the meeting MAY require the A/E to bring:

options.A: Design drawings, references, product literature, material ratings, and certifications
options.B: Sealed shop drawings and submittals prepared later by the contractor
options.C: Only the completed building permit application and its filing fee
options.D: Nothing at all in advance, since the AHJ already supplies every needed document on its own

questions.explanation: To describe the modification or interpretation being requested, the A/E may need to bring supporting material such as design drawings, references, product literature, material ratings, and product certifications. Contractor submittals or just a permit application would not adequately make the case.

questions.question: Beyond knowing the codes governing a project, specifiers must also remain cognizant of:

options.A: The procurement method the owner will use to award the construction contract
options.B: The product representative's internal sales targets for the specified products
options.C: When the next version of the code becomes effective, according to the AHJ
options.D: The general contractor's preferred sequence for scheduling the project work

questions.explanation: Beyond knowing which codes apply, specifiers must also keep track of when the AHJ's next code edition takes effect, so the documents stay aligned with the correct edition. Procurement method, sales targets, and contractor scheduling are unrelated to that duty.

questions.question: A contractor submits a substitution request after the bid date. What is the A/E's primary obligation when evaluating it?

options.A: Forward salient characteristics to the manufacturer for its approval of equivalency
options.B: Determine whether the proposed product is equivalent in salient characteristics
options.C: Accept it as equivalent if its quoted price is lower than the specified product
options.D: Reject it because salient characteristics cannot be evaluated after the bid date

questions.explanation: The core of any substitution review is judging whether the offered product matches the specified one in its defining (salient) characteristics. The A/E performs that comparison; equivalency is not delegated to the manufacturer, and price alone never establishes it.

questions.question: In a design-build project where the design-builder hires the contractor, which procurement option is most commonly used?

options.A: The competitive-bid option, awarded to the low responsive bid
options.B: The competitive-proposal option, scored on stated criteria
options.C: The sealed-proposal option, opened publicly at a fixed time
options.D: The negotiation option, with a contractor they already know

questions.explanation: Design-builders most often select construction partners by negotiation, since they tend to engage firms with whom they have an existing working relationship rather than opening the work to competitive bidding.

questions.question: ASTM E2112, Standard Practice for Installation of Exterior Windows, Doors and Skylights, is best classified as which type of reference standard?

options.A: Workmanship standard
options.B: Performance standard
options.C: Test method standard
options.D: Design standard

questions.explanation: Because E2112 governs how the work is installed rather than how a product is tested or designed, it falls into the workmanship category of reference standards.

questions.question: Which factor is LEAST appropriate as a basis for accepting a value-engineering substitution?

options.A: A lower purchase price even though it adds project coordination cost
options.B: Equivalent specified performance achieved at a measurably lower first cost
options.C: Equal aesthetic result with measurably reduced long-term maintenance cost
options.D: Comparable quality and performance with a shorter delivery lead time

questions.explanation: A cheaper price by itself cannot justify a product that no longer meets the required performance. Sound value analysis weighs quality, performance, budget, and schedule together, so a savings offset by added coordination cost is the weakest basis for acceptance.

questions.question: Critical performance features of equipment (e.g., valve pressure rating) are best verified through:

options.A: Manufacturer marketing literature and published sales brochures alone
options.B: Substitution requests submitted by the contractor after the award
options.C: Testing and code-required certifications confirming the rating
options.D: Visual inspection of representative samples during the design stage

questions.explanation: Many critical ratings cannot be confirmed simply by looking at a product. They have to be established through testing and the certifications required by code, which is what assures the owner the product actually complies.

questions.question: A product fails to comply with an applicable safety code. The product should be:

options.A: Accepted if it has a manufacturer warranty
options.B: Approved as a substitution at the contractor's risk
options.C: Excluded from the project
options.D: Listed as an alternate

questions.explanation: If a product does not satisfy an applicable code or a specified standard, it has no place in the project and should be left out, regardless of other attributes.

questions.question: Which is the preferred way to note a roof membrane on contract drawings?

options.A: A generic note such as 'roof membrane' keyed to the specifications
options.B: Manufacturer name and proprietary product number placed on the drawing
options.C: Detailed membrane installation instructions lettered onto the plan view
options.D: Performance criteria for the membrane noted directly on the roof drawing

questions.explanation: Drawings should carry only short generic identifiers (for example, 'roof membrane' or a type designation), leaving the full product description and requirements to the specifications.

questions.question: MasterFormat division and section titles are intended to:

options.A: Assign scope of work to specific trade subcontractors on the project
options.B: Organize specification information, not to assign work to trades
options.C: Assign work to specific construction trades performing the labor
options.D: Establish the required construction sequence among the trades

questions.explanation: MasterFormat exists to organize how specification content is arranged. It is not a tool for dividing scope among trades, and subcontractor boundaries should not dictate how sections are structured.

questions.question: When the time allotted for value analysis is limited, the most likely consequence is:

options.A: More thorough product evaluation despite the compressed design schedule
options.B: Reduced substitution requests because the design is locked in earlier
options.C: Lower overall construction cost because fewer alternatives are priced
options.D: Fewer options evaluated, raising substitution requests in construction

questions.explanation: Compressing the time for value analysis means the A/E studies fewer alternatives during design. The unexamined options then tend to resurface as substitution requests once construction is underway, frequently driving costs up.

questions.question: If two cited reference standards conflict with one another, the most reliable A/E response is to:

options.A: Identify the conflict and modify the spec to remove the contradiction
options.B: Add a clause that the more stringent of the conflicting standards governs
options.C: Default to the older standard whenever the conflict cannot be reconciled
options.D: Let the contractor resolve the conflict by selecting which one applies

questions.explanation: Conflicts between cited standards need to be spotted and reconciled directly in the specifications. A catch-all 'more stringent governs' clause is unreliable because it cannot untangle every kind of conflict.

questions.question: Under the CMAR project delivery method, who typically prepares the procurement documents for each subcontract?

options.A: The owner, acting through its own in-house purchasing staff
options.B: The A/E, as the design professional of record
options.C: The construction manager holding the trade contracts
options.D: The bonding agent furnishing the surety bonds

questions.explanation: In CMAR the procurement documents for each trade package are produced by the construction manager who issues that package, not by the A/E.

questions.question: Where two codes cover the same product with overlapping but non-identical requirements, the A/E must:

options.A: Always require full simultaneous compliance with both of the codes at once
options.B: Allow the contractor to choose whichever overlapping code is easier
options.C: Default to the older code because it is the more established option
options.D: Know which standard is referenced and which aspects each code covers

questions.explanation: When two codes overlap on the same product, the A/E has to understand exactly which aspects each one addresses and which standard the specifications actually invoke, rather than blindly demanding compliance with both or deferring the choice.

questions.question: Product evaluation in the design phase is best characterized as:

options.A: A multi-phased, progressive evaluation continuing through the design phases
options.B: A design evaluation performed only when value engineering is requested
options.C: A single design evaluation made at the start of construction documents
options.D: A design evaluation that is solely the contractor's submittal-phase responsibility

questions.explanation: Evaluating products is an ongoing, staged activity. It starts in schematic design and keeps developing as the design gains detail through each successive phase, rather than happening at a single point.

questions.question: Why should equipment such as pumps or valves be identified on drawings by short generic names or codes (e.g., 'PRV-1')?

options.A: To satisfy MasterFormat section-numbering rules that apply to drawings
options.B: To simplify drawing changes by keeping descriptions in the specs
options.C: To assist the AHJ in enforcing code provisions during the plan review
options.D: To prevent contractors from proposing any unauthorized substitutions

questions.explanation: Short codes and symbols keep the detailed descriptions in the specifications, so if a product changes, fewer edits are needed on the drawings themselves.

questions.question: Legally, the difference between 'guaranty' and 'warranty' is best described as:

options.A: A guaranty is a third party's separate contract; a warranty is the principal's assurance
options.B: Only warranties may ever be written; a guaranty is always an oral assurance given
options.C: They are legally identical and remain fully interchangeable in every legal context
options.D: A guaranty is always shorter in its duration than any manufacturer's product warranty held

questions.explanation: In legal terms a guaranty is a separate undertaking by a third party (comparable to a surety bond) to answer for another's obligation, while a warranty is the principal party's own assurance about the responsibilities it has taken on.

questions.question: Why should drawings avoid cross-references such as 'refer to specifications'?

options.A: Drawings and specs are complementary, so broad cross-references are discouraged
options.B: Drawings may not legally cross-reference any other contract document at all
options.C: Such cross-references are confidential and must be withheld from the contractor
options.D: Cross-references imply the specs take legal precedence over the drawings

questions.explanation: Drawings and specifications complement each other within one contract set, so sweeping pointers like 'see specifications' add little and are discouraged. Citing a specific section number, however, is acceptable.

questions.question: When evaluating systems for a project, the A/E should generally:

options.A: Evaluate the small components first before considering any systems
options.B: Evaluate components and whole systems independently of one another
options.C: Evaluate major systems and subsystems first, then smaller components
options.D: Defer all of the system selections entirely until the contractor is engaged

questions.explanation: Because major system choices constrain everything that follows, the A/E should settle the large systems and subsystems first, then select smaller components for compatibility with those earlier decisions.

questions.question: Limited time for product evaluation in design most often leads to which downstream effect?

options.A: Improved schedule performance from making earlier design decisions
options.B: Lower construction cost from a more streamlined final product list
options.C: Fewer addenda because fewer products are evaluated during design
options.D: An increase in substitution requests during the construction stage

questions.explanation: When there is little time for value analysis, fewer alternatives get studied during design, and the gaps tend to show up later as substitution requests during construction, often pushing prices higher.

questions.question: A pressurized force-main system must withstand 250 psi. The owner's assurance of compliance for the seals depends primarily on:

options.A: Visual inspection for compliance during the site installation
options.B: Compliance with the applicable code and referenced standards
options.C: The supplier's quoted price as evidence of compliance
options.D: The A/E's professional judgment of compliance, unaided by testing

questions.explanation: A pressure rating like this cannot be confirmed by looking at the parts. The owner's confidence that the seals perform comes from the components meeting the referenced code requirements and standards.

questions.question: Which factor most directly establishes price parameters for product selection during value analysis?

options.A: The AHJ inspection schedule that is set for the project's review
options.B: The trade affiliation of the installer doing the work
options.C: The MasterFormat section title assigned to the product
options.D: Budget requirements and the product's maintenance costs

questions.explanation: The project budget together with a product's expected maintenance costs is what sets the price boundaries that guide selection during value analysis.

questions.question: An A/E discovers that the manufacturer's roof warranty excludes damage from winds at 55 mph peak gust, but the code requires design for 70 mph sustained / 85 mph gust. What should the A/E do?

options.A: Accept the warranty as written, since the manufacturer's terms govern
options.B: Reduce the code-required wind design to match the warranty limit
options.C: Require the warranty be modified to meet code or select another product
options.D: Issue an addendum reducing the project's specified design wind loads instead

questions.explanation: Warranty limits have to be checked against code-required performance. A warranty that caps coverage below the code-mandated wind load is unacceptable, so the A/E must have it revised to meet code or choose a different product.

questions.question: In value analysis, the 'value' of a building element is best understood as the relationship between:

options.A: The contractor’s profit margin and the initial purchase price
options.B: The function or performance it delivers and the life cycle cost to achieve that function
options.C: Its aesthetic appeal and the owner’s personal preference
options.D: The construction schedule duration and the labor hours required

questions.explanation: Value analysis improves value by maximizing the ratio of function (the performance an element must deliver) to the life cycle cost of providing it. The goal is the lowest total cost of ownership that still meets the required function—not the lowest first cost, and not aesthetics or schedule in isolation.
questions.source: value analysis and life cycle cost

questions.question: In integrated project delivery (IPD), the construction documentation process most closely resembles which other delivery method?

options.A: Design-bid-build with a single competitive-bid construction package
options.B: Owner-build, with the owner self-performing all documentation
options.C: CMAR, using fast-track scheduling and multiple work packages
options.D: Developer-led design-build under a single negotiated contract

questions.explanation: Regardless of how IPD is contracted, its documentation workflow tends to mirror CMAR, relying on fast-track scheduling and a series of work packages.

questions.question: In the design-bid-build negotiated option, when is the project manual typically completed?

options.A: It is not produced at all for the negotiated delivery option
options.B: Before schematic design phase work begins on the project
options.C: After negotiations begin, during the early design phases
options.D: Only after the construction contract is fully signed

questions.explanation: Under the negotiated option the project manual comes together once negotiations are underway, often built up from outline specifications that work toward a guaranteed maximum price.

questions.question: If a substitution affects other specified products, what action is typically required?

options.A: The A/E rejects the substitution outright and requires the base specified product
options.B: The contractor assumes responsibility for the added coordination at no owner cost
options.C: No further action is needed as long as the substitution itself complies
options.D: The owner negotiates a separate side agreement with the manufacturer

questions.explanation: Standard substitution procedures put the burden on the contractor to cover the cost of coordinating any changes to related work that an accepted substitution causes.

questions.question: Constructability evaluation primarily aims to:

options.A: Eliminate shop drawings entirely once the constructability review is done
options.B: Reduce the size of the project manual through the constructability review
options.C: Assign trade scope using MasterFormat numbering during the evaluation process itself
options.D: Coordinate design, product evaluation, and construction into a workable sequence

questions.explanation: A constructability evaluation brings design, product selection, and construction together so the work can be carried out in a sequence that satisfies the project's requirements.

questions.question: ASTM C150 covers ten cement types. If the A/E does not specify the type, the selection is:

options.A: Made by the AHJ, which selects the cement type during the plan review
options.B: Determined by the testing laboratory based on its field sampling
options.C: Forfeited to the contractor, who tends to pick the cheapest type
options.D: Defaulted to Type I, which ASTM C150 designates as the standard

questions.explanation: When a standard contains internal options (such as the several cement types in ASTM C150), the A/E must pin down the choice. Leaving it open hands the decision to the contractor, who will usually take the least costly option.

questions.question: Value analysis primarily seeks to identify:

options.A: Cost savings and benefits for evaluation by the project team
options.B: Potential contract-law exposure arising from the specifications
options.C: The construction trades responsible for each specification section
options.D: Code violations embedded in the project specifications

questions.explanation: The purpose of value analysis is to surface opportunities for cost savings and other benefits that the project team can then weigh.

questions.question: When a basis-of-design product is specified, the specification should:

options.A: Prohibit every substitution so that only the one named product is acceptable
options.B: Describe the salient characteristics so equivalents are judged for compliance
options.C: List only the single manufacturer's name and the model number for that product
options.D: Defer all of the product performance criteria to the contractor's selection

questions.explanation: A basis-of-design specification needs to spell out the product's salient characteristics so that proposed equivalents can be measured against them and judged for compliance.

questions.question: Which is NOT among the recognized liabilities of incorporating reference standards by citation?

options.A: Standards can contain embedded options
options.B: Different AHJs may enforce different editions of the same standard
options.C: Standards eliminate the need for the A/E to know the subject area
options.D: Inadequate standards may coexist with stringent ones

questions.explanation: Citing a standard never substitutes for the A/E's own command of the subject; in fact the A/E must read a standard closely before referencing it. So 'eliminating the need to know the subject' is not a real benefit, it is the answer that does not belong.

questions.question: When issuing multiple work packages under CMAR, Division 01 is best handled by:

options.A: Issuing it as a stand-alone package later packages reference
options.B: Issuing a full copy of Division 01 within each separate work package
options.C: Issuing the work packages with Division 01 omitted entirely
options.D: Issuing each subcontract with a CM-rewritten Division 01 set

questions.explanation: To avoid duplicating content across packages, Division 01 is best issued once as a stand-alone package that the later work packages refer back to; any revisions go out with the package they affect.

questions.question: When fast-tracking under the CM as advisor/agent method with multiple-prime contracts, the A/E's document preparation time will most likely:

options.A: Remain the same as it would for a single-prime design-bid-build
options.B: Be eliminated entirely, since the CM prepares all the documents
options.C: Decrease, because the overall project schedule is made shorter
options.D: Increase, even though the overall project schedule is reduced

questions.explanation: Fast-tracking with multiple-prime contracts shortens the overall project schedule, but it actually adds to the A/E's documentation workload because separate coordinated packages must be produced.

questions.question: Which warranty term is generally the LEAST reliable basis for comparing two warranties?

options.A: Duration alone
options.B: Exclusions and limitations
options.C: Manufacturer's financial backing
options.D: Whether labor is covered

questions.explanation: Length of coverage is the term people compare most, yet it may matter least. Looking only at duration gives no way to weed out weaker coverage hidden in exclusions, conditions, or labor terms.

questions.question: Which document section should typically govern the procedures for evaluating substitution requests?

options.A: The Conditions of the Contract, taken on their own
options.B: Division 00 procurement requirements issued for bidding
options.C: The applicable technical specification section for the product
options.D: Division 01 General Requirements, Section 01 25 00

questions.explanation: Substitution procedures are administered out of Division 01, most often through Section 01 25 00 Substitution Procedures, which sets out how requests are made and evaluated.

questions.question: Which statement about construction warranties is correct?

options.A: They are governed exclusively by the Uniform Commercial Code alone
options.B: They run concurrently with, and in addition to, the general warranty
options.C: They eliminate any need for a separate manufacturer's product warranty
options.D: They replace the contractor's one-year correction-period obligation

questions.explanation: Warranties specified for particular materials and equipment do not displace the contractor's general warranty or correction-period duties; they layer on top of them, running at the same time and in addition to them.

questions.question: Reference standards in a specification should be:

options.A: Reviewed for currency and applicability before incorporation
options.B: Used verbatim regardless of the actual project requirements
options.C: Replaced by manufacturer literature wherever that is possible
options.D: Cited by title only, without giving any edition or date

questions.explanation: Before a standard is folded into a specification, the A/E should confirm its content and intent and make sure it actually fits the project at hand.

questions.question: A product with a long lead time is being considered. The A/E should primarily evaluate:

options.A: The complexity of the required shop drawings for it
options.B: Whether the product has a national distributor network
options.C: The range of color options offered for the product
options.D: How the product's delivery fits the project schedule

questions.explanation: Availability and delivery timing are schedule considerations in value analysis. For a long-lead item, the key question is whether its delivery can be reconciled with the project schedule.

questions.question: Off-site (shop) fabrication is typically beneficial when:

options.A: Field conditions are better controlled than the shop conditions
options.B: The product is too small to transport to the site efficiently
options.C: Shop conditions allow better quality control before delivery
options.D: Field labor is the only construction resource that is available

questions.explanation: Moving work into a shop, where conditions can be controlled more tightly before the item ships to the site, often benefits the owner through better quality.

questions.question: Considering how project decisions affect total project cost over time, the ability to influence cost is GREATEST during which phase?

options.A: Bidding and the procurement phase of project work
options.B: Programming and the schematic design phase
options.C: Construction documents production phase
options.D: Construction phase, on the building site

questions.explanation: The leverage a decision has over total project cost is highest at the very start and drops off steeply as work proceeds. The earliest phases (programming and schematic design) are where choices shape outcomes most, while later changes cost far more to make.

questions.question: In Design-Bid-Build (DBB) delivery, which direct contractual relationship does NOT exist?

options.A: Owner-A/E
options.B: Direct A/E-contractor
options.C: Contractor-subcontractor
options.D: Owner-contractor

questions.explanation: DBB is built on two separate prime contracts: one between the owner and the A/E, and one between the owner and the contractor. The A/E and the contractor have no contract with each other and instead communicate through the owner.

questions.question: In Construction Management at Risk (CMAR), the construction manager typically:

options.A: Is hired by and contracts directly with the A/E for the work
options.B: Holds the subcontracts and assumes cost/schedule risk under a GMP
options.C: Acts only as the owner's advisor and so carries no contractual risk
options.D: Replaces the A/E and self-performs the project design services

questions.explanation: In CMAR the construction manager moves from a preconstruction advisory role into the role of constructor who carries risk. The CM usually holds the trade subcontracts and commits to a guaranteed maximum price for the work.

questions.question: In Design-Build (DB) delivery, the owner contracts with:

options.A: A separate A/E firm and a separate construction contractor entity
options.B: A construction manager only, who in turn hires the project design team here
options.C: Subcontractors directly, with no single intermediary entity in between
options.D: A single entity that provides both the design and the construction

questions.explanation: Design-Build gives the owner one agreement with a single design-build entity that carries responsibility for both designing and building the project.

questions.question: In Integrated Project Delivery (IPD), the relationship among owner, A/E, and contractor is typically:

options.A: A single design-build agreement holding both design and build
options.B: Two separate prime agreements managed independently of each other
options.C: A series of bilateral two-party agreements among the parties
options.D: A multi-party agreement with shared risk and shared reward

questions.explanation: IPD aligns the owner, A/E, and contractor under a single multi-party agreement that ties them together with shared risk, shared reward, and collaboration that begins early in the project.

questions.question: Two codes apply to panic hardware: ICC requires a maximum 15-lb operating force; California Building Code requires 5 lb. The specifier must:

options.A: Average the two hardware operating forces (10 lb) for compliance
options.B: Specify hardware meeting the 15-lb ICC value as the baseline code
options.C: Specify hardware meeting the more stringent 5-lb requirement
options.D: Leave the choice of hardware operating force to the contractor

questions.explanation: When two codes overlap, the stricter requirement controls. The 5-lb limit is the more restrictive of the two, so hardware must meet it in order to satisfy both codes at once.

questions.question: For a natatorium (indoor pool) building enclosure, the MOST important product-evaluation consideration is:

options.A: Energy code compliance, evaluated entirely on its own
options.B: Low acoustic absorption of the enclosure assemblies
options.C: Specular reflectivity of surfaces for interior daylighting
options.D: Resistance to fading and corrosion from chlorine vapors

questions.explanation: Indoor pool spaces fill with chlorine-laden vapor that attacks finishes, fading and corroding them. The leading selection criterion for that environment is therefore a material's resistance to fading and corrosion.

questions.question: The MOST important environmental consideration when selecting finish materials for a sauna is:

options.A: Light reflectance value of the interior sauna finish surfaces
options.B: Tolerance of sustained high temperature and intermittent moisture
options.C: Acoustic absorption used to control reverberation in the room
options.D: Low VOC emissions from the installed interior wall finish materials

questions.explanation: Saunas subject materials to long stretches of high heat combined with bursts of high moisture. Finishes there must be specifically rated to withstand that paired exposure.

questions.question: For a weight room (free weights, dropped equipment), the MOST important product evaluation consideration is typically:

options.A: Floor finish impact resistance and resilience
options.B: The interior wall paint sheen and gloss level
options.C: The ceiling acoustic panel selection and type
options.D: The window U-factor and thermal performance

questions.explanation: In a weight room the floor takes repeated punishment from dropped weights, so the dominant selection criteria are the floor finish's impact resistance, resilience, and ability to damp noise.

questions.question: For a low-slope roof on a Gulf Coast office building, which membrane color is generally preferred and why?

options.A: Color is irrelevant to roof performance in any hot, humid climate
options.B: Gray, because the energy codes mandate a neutral default color
options.C: Black, because a dark membrane sheds rainwater more quickly off it
options.D: White or light-reflective, to cut solar heat gain and cooling load

questions.explanation: In a hot climate a light or highly reflective membrane reflects solar energy, trimming heat gain and cooling demand. Many energy codes encourage or require such reflective roofing.

questions.question: Constructability evaluation is BEST described as a review to determine whether the project:

options.A: Will be built efficiently and in sequence with available resources
options.B: Will be delivered within the owner's established construction budget
options.C: Complies fully with every applicable building and fire-safety code
options.D: Satisfies the program and functional requirements set by the owner

questions.explanation: A constructability review asks whether the documents let the work be built in a sensible sequence using ordinary construction methods and the resources that are actually available.

questions.question: When evaluating exterior window systems against project performance criteria, the specifier should:

options.A: Select against cost alone among the otherwise compliant manufacturers
options.B: Compare independently tested air, water, structural, and thermal data
options.C: Defer the criteria evaluation to the contractor's post-award submittals
options.D: Accept any product the manufacturer claims meets the project criteria

questions.explanation: Windows should be judged on independently tested performance data — air infiltration (e.g., ASTM E283), water penetration (e.g., ASTM E331), plus structural and thermal results — measured against the project's stated criteria, rather than on cost or unverified manufacturer claims.

questions.question: Compared to DBB with competitive bid, Division 00 for DBB with the competitive proposal option typically:

options.A: Eliminates the proposal documents entirely under this delivery option
options.B: Adds a guaranteed-maximum-price exhibit attached to the proposal set
options.C: Replaces the Bid Form with a Proposal Form and adds evaluation criteria
options.D: Requires no instructions to proposers at all because the pricing is left open

questions.explanation: Switching to the competitive proposal option swaps the strict bid documents for a Proposal Form and a set of proposal-evaluation criteria, and it allows some negotiation. Bonds and the rest of Division 00 still apply.

questions.question: Adding an additional performance criterion (e.g., hurricane impact rating) to a product evaluation matrix MOST often:

options.A: Eliminates the need for substitution procedures
options.B: Has no effect on the number of compliant products
options.C: Reduces the number of compliant products
options.D: Increases the number of compliant products

questions.explanation: Every added criterion acts as another filter on the candidate set, so stacking criteria usually shrinks the pool of fully compliant products and can point toward a basis-of-design approach.

questions.question: In a large gathering space, the MOST effective approach to control reverberation and improve speech intelligibility is to:

options.A: Add acoustic panels and absorptive finishes, limiting hard reflective surfaces
options.B: Specify hard, reflective surfaces throughout to project the sound farther
options.C: Specify thicker masonry party walls to block sound transmission between the rooms
options.D: Increase the ceiling height substantially with no added acoustic treatment

questions.explanation: Reverberation in a large room is best tamed by introducing sound-absorbing finishes — acoustic panels, fabric, carpet — while cutting back on hard, reflective surfaces.

questions.question: For a Gulf Coast project, which is the MOST critical initial consideration for the contractor when planning product procurement and installation?

options.A: Local labor-union jurisdictions governing each of the installing trades
options.B: Construction-phase exposure to hurricane season, staging accordingly
options.C: Federal Buy American compliance for all of the procured materials
options.D: The owner's preferred electronic submittal and transmittal file format

questions.explanation: On a hurricane-prone coast the contractor's first planning concern is seasonal storm risk: protecting in-progress work, staging high-value materials wisely, and building in weather-related schedule contingencies. A common consequence is the push to install the roof early and dry the building in before peak season.

questions.question: In Integrated Project Delivery (IPD), a Single-Purpose Entity (SPE) is BEST described as:

options.A: A single entity that is the contractor's sole-source specialty sub
options.B: A single entity formed by owner, A/E, and contractor sharing risk/reward
options.C: A single entity that is a subsidiary owned solely by the project owner
options.D: A single entity that is a design-build firm holding both of the contracts

questions.explanation: An IPD Single-Purpose Entity is a legal entity that the owner, A/E, and contractor create jointly for the project so they can share its financial risk and reward. It is one of several contractual forms IPD can take.

questions.question: In an Owner-Build (force-account) delivery, the owner's coordination obligations differ from DBB primarily because:

options.A: The owner is also the constructor and assumes the contractor's coordination role
options.B: The owner provides all in-house design and its own coordination services
options.C: Substantial completion and its coordination milestone are not declared on Owner-Build
options.D: Only Division 01 coordination requirements apply in the project manual

questions.explanation: In Owner-Build the owner performs the construction (or directs its own forces) and therefore takes on the coordination and quality-control duties a contractor would normally carry. The A/E typically still works under contract to the owner, and many Division 01 provisions continue to apply.

questions.question: Construction Manager as Advisor (CMa) and Construction Manager as Agent are most reliably distinguished by:

options.A: Whether the project is delivered using a guaranteed maximum price arrangement
options.B: Whether the CM has delegated authority to make binding owner decisions
options.C: Whether the CM holds the trade contracts (Agent does, Advisor does not hold any)
options.D: Whether the CM provides any preconstruction advisory services before construction

questions.explanation: Both the advisor and the agent forms contract only with the owner; neither holds the trade contracts (that is CMAR). What sets the agent apart is delegated authority: an agent can make binding decisions on the owner's behalf, whereas an advisor only advises.

questions.question: On a six-scope project the owner signs separate prime contracts for site, general, masonry, mechanical, plumbing, and electrical work. Unless the documents assign coordination authority to a contractual entity, who most likely bears coordination responsibility?

options.A: The owner, who assumes that duty by default when none is designated
options.B: The architect/engineer, by virtue of having produced all the documents
options.C: The masonry contractor, as the trade the other primes build upon
options.D: The largest prime by value, whose scope drives the overall schedule

questions.explanation: If no contractual party is given coordination authority, the owner generally ends up responsible for coordinating among the multiple primes. This differs from single-prime delivery, where one contractor coordinates its own subcontractors.

questions.question: Compared with single-prime delivery, the division of work and coordination burden under multiple-prime delivery differs in that:

options.A: The A/E divides the work into subcontracts and the one contractor coordinates
options.B: The owner or its CM defines the work split and bears the coordination risk
options.C: Each prime sequences only its own scope, so no central party is required
options.D: The contractor divides the work into subcontracts and coordinates it all

questions.explanation: With multiple primes, the party defining how the work splits among contracts (the A/E, the CM, or the owner-builder) also shoulders the coordination risk; careful coordination is essential and inter-contract claims are common. The option describing one contractor dividing the work and coordinating it all is really single-prime delivery.

questions.question: For a multiple-prime project, the A/E's preparation of construction documents most commonly differs from single-prime in that the A/E:

options.A: Prepares a separate document set per prime, each summarizing that extent
options.B: Hands document preparation to the lowest qualified prime for each scope
options.C: Omits Division 01, since each prime supplies its own general requirements
options.D: Issues one combined project manual applying identically to every prime

questions.explanation: Because different contractors handle different portions of a multiple-prime project, the A/E may produce a distinct document set for each contract, each with a clear summary of that contract's extent.

questions.question: Multiple-prime contracts most frequently arise from which scheduling approach, and carry which recognized cost consequence?

options.A: Fast-track scheduling, with detailed coordination adding to project cost
options.B: Linear sequencing, with reduced documentation cost from consolidating scopes
options.C: Critical-path scheduling, removing any need for construction management
options.D: Phased occupancy, with all coordination risk passed to the subcontractors

questions.explanation: Multiple-prime arrangements often grow out of fast-track scheduling, and the close coordination of documents and contracts they demand can add cost. Large or complex projects of this kind frequently call for construction management.

questions.question: On a multiple-prime project, how should each prime contractor's scope be delineated graphically versus in writing?

options.A: Both the graphic limits and the binding scope wording appear on the drawings
options.B: Graphics may show separate contracts, but scope belongs in Div 01 and PART 1
options.C: Scope is fixed only by MasterFormat section titles, controlling trade work
options.D: Each prime marks its own scope limits on an independent record drawing set

questions.explanation: Drawings can show the limits of separate contracts graphically, but the binding written scope-of-work language belongs in Division 01 and in the PART 1 - GENERAL portion of the specification sections.

questions.question: Why do large or complex multiple-prime projects often require construction management, when a comparable single-prime project may not?

options.A: Multiple-prime contracts cannot be fast-tracked unless a CM holds contracts
options.B: Construction management is legally mandated when more than one trade is on site
options.C: No single contractor coordinates the primes, so inter-contract claims arise
options.D: The A/E is contractually barred from providing contract administration here

questions.explanation: Under multiple-prime delivery no single contractor coordinates the separate primes, making coordination critical and inter-contract claims likely. That gap is why these projects so often bring in construction management.

questions.question: An owner wants single-point construction-cost responsibility via a guaranteed maximum price while still getting major-trade input during design. Which method provides this and how?

options.A: CM as advisor, where the advisor binds the owner to the negotiated GMP
options.B: CMAR, where the manager holds the risk and gives a GMP after design input
options.C: Design-bid-build competitive bid, where the low bid becomes the fixed sum
options.D: Multiple-prime, where each prime guarantees a maximum price for its scope

questions.explanation: CMAR fits because the at-risk manager participates during design and then provides a guaranteed maximum price, giving the owner a single accountable party for cost. A CM-Advisor cannot bind the owner, and DBB sets price only after the documents are complete.

questions.question: In design-bid-build, the architect/engineer and the contractor stand in what relationship to one another?

options.A: No contractual relationship at all, but rather an administrative relationship during the work
options.B: A subcontract relationship in which the contractor reports to and is directed by the A/E
options.C: A contractual relationship established indirectly through the owner-architect/engineer agreement
options.D: A multi-party agreement under which they share project-level risk and reward with the owner

questions.explanation: Because the owner contracts separately with the A/E and with the contractor, those two parties have no contract between them; their dealings during construction are purely administrative. This linear arrangement is what defines DBB.

questions.question: Why is CMAR increasingly acceptable for public work despite the constructor's early design involvement?

options.A: Public competitive-bidding laws are fully waived the moment any construction manager is retained
options.B: The CM competed to become the CMAR and subcontractors competed for work, preserving competition
options.C: The CMAR contractually guarantees the absolute lowest first cost obtainable on every subcontract
options.D: The architect/engineer assumes the construction risk, so the public agency carries none of it

questions.explanation: CMAR keeps competition intact even with early constructor involvement: the construction manager won the CMAR role competitively, and the subcontractors competed for their work. That preserves the public agency's duty of care over taxpayer funds.

questions.question: Negotiated design-bid-build contracts are rarely used for publicly funded projects mainly because:

options.A: Public owners typically lack staff experienced enough to negotiate a construction contract
options.B: A negotiated contract is legally incapable of incorporating a guaranteed maximum price clause
options.C: Competitive-bidding laws bar starting construction before the final construction cost is known
options.D: The architect/engineer is statutorily barred from administering any negotiated public contract

questions.explanation: Public competitive-bidding laws generally forbid beginning construction until the final cost is established, which is what makes negotiated DBB rare on public work. An exception can arise where project complexity limits the pool of qualified bidders.

questions.question: Which statement best captures how integrated project delivery (IPD) manages risk, distinct from traditional methods?

options.A: The owner retains essentially all risk and indemnifies the other parties
options.B: A multi-party agreement focuses risk management at the project level
options.C: Risk is allocated to each participant so each bears only its own scope
options.D: Risk is transferred to a surety through a three-party guaranty bond set

questions.explanation: IPD handles risk at the level of the whole project rather than parceling it out to individual participants. Its multi-party agreement typically pairs a no-blame culture and liability waivers with risk and reward shared according to overall outcomes.

questions.question: The MacLeamy Curve is most often cited to support which premise underlying IPD?

options.A: Design decisions should shift earlier, when impact is high and change cost low
options.B: Construction waste can be minimized only by extending the construction time
options.C: The cost of design changes reaches its lowest point during construction
options.D: The architect/engineer's fee should be weighted toward construction administration

questions.explanation: This curve is used to argue for moving design decisions earlier in the timeline, to the point where the ability to affect cost and function is greatest and the cost of making changes is still low.

questions.question: A single-purpose entity (SPE) created for a construction project differs from a typical real-estate SPE in that the construction SPE:

options.A: Holds legal title to a single income-producing property throughout its life
options.B: Will have no assets of its own and is dissolved when the project completes
options.C: Is a permanent corporation that survives to pursue future similar ventures
options.D: May be used only for design-bid-build, never for design-build or IPD work

questions.explanation: Unlike a real-estate SPE that holds a single property as its asset, a construction SPE owns no assets of its own. It is set up for the one project and dissolved at completion, and it is used in design-build and IPD.

questions.question: An IPD single-purpose entity typically involves which membership, distinguishing it from a design-build SPE?

options.A: Only the contractor and the architect/engineer serving as its owner-managers
options.B: The owner paired with a surety acting as the guarantor of all performance
options.C: A tri-party agreement among owner, contractor, and architect/engineer
options.D: The owner acting alone, who later assigns membership to selected subs

questions.explanation: An IPD SPE usually rests on a three-party agreement that includes the owner, contractor, and A/E. A design-build SPE, by contrast, is typically owned or managed just by a contractor and an A/E.

questions.question: A construction manager as agent (CM-Agent) is distinguished from a CM as advisor (CM-Advisor) chiefly in that the CM-Agent:

options.A: Contracts with the A/E, while the CM-Advisor contracts with the contractor
options.B: Enters into the trade subcontracts directly, whereas the Advisor holds none
options.C: Guarantees the cost of the work, while the CM-Advisor guarantees schedule
options.D: Can make and render decisions binding on the owner, which Advisor cannot

questions.explanation: The agent form carries delegated authority to make decisions that bind the owner, while the advisor form may only counsel. Neither one contracts with the trades; both contract solely with the owner.

questions.question: Under the CM-Agent method, which is NOT a characteristic of the construction manager's position?

options.A: Guaranteeing and being directly responsible for delays and cost overruns
options.B: Acting as the owner's agent, with authority defined by the owner agreement
options.C: Entering into agreements only with the owner, not with any contractors
options.D: Making and rendering decisions binding on the owner within delegated limits

questions.explanation: A CM-Agent does not guarantee construction outcomes or bear direct responsibility for delays, overruns, and defects. It serves as the owner's agent, contracts only with the owner, and binds the owner within its delegated authority — so the guarantee of delays and overruns is the trait that does not fit.

questions.question: In design-build delivery, the owner's single-point responsibility comes at the cost of which trade-off relative to design-bid-build?

options.A: The owner gains an enforceable contractual relationship directly between the A/E and contractor
options.B: The owner must personally coordinate among several separate prime construction contracts
options.C: The owner gives up the independent A/E whose design loyalty in DBB runs solely to the owner
options.D: The owner forfeits any ability to use a guaranteed maximum price on the construction work

questions.explanation: In DBB the owner holds a separate contract with an independent A/E whose allegiance runs only to the owner. Design-build folds design and construction into one entity, so the owner trades single-point responsibility for the loss of that independent advocate.

questions.question: A contractor providing design-assist services and ultimately presenting a guaranteed maximum price during design is most characteristic of which arrangement?

options.A: The design-bid-build competitive bid option, in which price is fixed by sealed low bid
options.B: Multiple-prime delivery, in which the owner separately contracts each defined scope of work
options.C: Owner-build (force-account) delivery, in which the owner supplies its own construction labor
options.D: The design-bid-build negotiation option or CMAR, pricing incomplete information toward a GMP

questions.explanation: Having a contractor assist the A/E, price still-incomplete information, and offer a guaranteed maximum price is the hallmark of the negotiated DBB option, and design-assist with a GMP is likewise central to CMAR.

questions.question: A design-bid-build project switches from the competitive bid option to the competitive proposal option. How does Division 00 most accurately change?

options.A: Equivalent proposal forms and documents replace the bidding forms and documents
options.B: Many of the forms and documents in the procurement requirements become needless
options.C: Division 00 does not change in any significant way under these circumstances
options.D: Division 00 is replaced entirely by the Division 01 general-requirements set

questions.explanation: Moving to the proposal option means the bidding forms and documents in Division 00 give way to their proposal-based equivalents, rather than disappearing or being replaced by Division 01.

questions.question: Under the design-bid-build competitive proposal option, after a proposer is selected, may the owner and contractor negotiate the contract's final price?

options.A: No, the proposed price becomes the fixed contract sum and may not afterward be negotiated
options.B: Yes, the owner and the selected contractor may negotiate the final price after selection
options.C: No, applicable public-bidding law forbids any negotiation once a proposer is selected
options.D: Only the architect/engineer, not the owner, may negotiate the final price after selection

questions.explanation: Unlike the strict low-bid option, the proposal option lets the owner and the chosen contractor negotiate the final contract price once the proposer has been selected.

questions.question: On which delivery method does the construction manager, rather than the A/E, prepare the procurement documents?

options.A: Design-bid-build, where the A/E completes the documents before procurement
options.B: Owner-build, where the owner's own staff prepares procurement documents always
options.C: Integrated project delivery, where the A/E prepares the documents in every case
options.D: Construction manager at risk (CMAR), where the CM prepares the packages

questions.explanation: CMAR is the method in which the construction manager, not the A/E, prepares the procurement documents for the subcontract packages — the reverse of DBB, where the A/E prepares them.

questions.question: For a CMAR project, how might project-manual preparation differ from traditional design-bid-build?

options.A: There is essentially no notable difference between a CMAR and a DBB manual
options.B: Decisions normally the A/E's alone may be shared with the owner and the CM
options.C: A single project manual is mandatory and may never be split into packages
options.D: Conditions of the contract are omitted, being established before the manual

questions.explanation: On a CMAR project, choices that would ordinarily rest with the A/E alone can be shared among team members, including the owner and the CM, and more than one project manual may be needed.

questions.question: For a design-build project, who prepares the procurement and contracting requirements used to obtain bids from the trades?

options.A: The owner, who issues the procurement requirements directly to the trade bidders
options.B: The authority having jurisdiction, as part of its review of the procurement package
options.C: The design-builder, who controls both the design and the construction procurement
options.D: A specifier the owner engages separately to prepare procurement requirements

questions.explanation: On a design-build project the design-builder prepares the procurement and contracting requirements, since it controls both the design and the procurement of construction.

questions.question: For an owner-build (force-account) project, is there a need to develop procurement requirements?

options.A: No, because the owner provides its own construction services, removing the need
options.B: Yes, because owner-build still requires the same procurement requirements as DBB
options.C: No, because the architect/engineer assumes the owner's construction role here
options.D: Yes, but only the bid-bond and performance-bond forms must be developed for it

questions.explanation: Because the owner supplies its own construction services in owner-build, there is no outside construction to procure, so procurement requirements are not needed.

questions.question: In most standard owner/design-builder agreements, how are the conditions of the contract handled?

options.A: They are issued as stand-alone documents bound into Division 00 of the manual
options.B: They are omitted entirely, since design-build requires no general conditions
options.C: They are prepared by the architect/engineer apart from the design-builder
options.D: They are incorporated into the agreement, so they do not appear separately

questions.explanation: Standard owner/design-builder agreements typically build the conditions of the contract into the agreement itself, so they are not issued as separate documents.

questions.question: Is Division 01 published for each separate work package on an integrated project delivery (IPD) project?

options.A: True, because a separate Division 01 must accompany every IPD work package
options.B: True, but only the general-requirements portion repeats for each package
options.C: False, because Division 01 is not published separately per IPD work package
options.D: False, because IPD delivery eliminates the Division 01 general requirements

questions.explanation: The claim that Division 01 must accompany every IPD work package is false. IPD's integrated structure does not call for republishing Division 01 with each separate package.

questions.question: A California high school gymnasium (occupant load 450) uses 36-inch-wide door leaves and needs touchpad panic hardware suited to that leaf and compliant with the California 5-pound force limit. The qualifying count depends on:

options.A: Only the ICC 15-pound operating-force limit, since ICC governs this project
options.B: The delayed-egress feature, treated as mandatory for educational occupancies
options.C: Whether each candidate device also includes the optional exit-alarm feature
options.D: The intersection of wide-stile suitability and CBC 5-pound force compliance

questions.explanation: A qualifying device has to satisfy two conditions at once: a wide-stile configuration suited to the 36-inch leaf AND compliance with the California 5-pound operating force. The qualifying set is the overlap of those two requirements, which screens out narrow-stile and non-5-pound models.

questions.question: Continuing the gymnasium panic-hardware evaluation, if hurricane testing is ADDED as a required criterion, what happens to the compliant-model count, given that every model already meeting the wide-stile and 5-pound criteria also carries a hurricane rating?

options.A: There is a decrease in the number of models that comply with all project requirements
options.B: There is an increase in the number of models that comply with all project requirements
options.C: There is no change in the number of models that comply with all project requirements
options.D: Every model becomes non-compliant once the hurricane criterion is added to the matrix

questions.explanation: Since every model that already passes the wide-stile and 5-pound tests also carries a hurricane rating, adding the hurricane criterion screens out nothing, so the compliant count is unchanged. Adding a criterion can only hold a count steady or lower it.

questions.question: As a general principle of product-evaluation counting, adding one more required criterion to an evaluation matrix has which possible effect on the number of compliant products?

options.A: It has no effect on the number of compliant products under any circumstances
options.B: It can only hold the count steady or decrease it; it can never increase it
options.C: It always reduces the count to exactly half of the previously compliant set
options.D: It can only increase the count, since more criteria capture more candidates

questions.explanation: Each additional required criterion narrows the qualifying set: products that already failed remain out, and some that passed may now fail. The compliant count can therefore stay the same or drop, but it can never rise.

questions.question: In the California gymnasium scenario, the local 5-pound maximum operating-force requirement governed over the ICC 15-pound requirement because:

options.A: Codes from any local jurisdiction automatically supersede every ICC rule
options.B: The ICC requirement simply does not apply to educational buildings at all
options.C: The 5-pound requirement is the more stringent of the two and so governs
options.D: The architect chose the lower figure arbitrarily to reduce design liability

questions.explanation: The 5-pound limit controls simply because it is the stricter of the two overlapping requirements; when two requirements both apply, the more stringent one governs.

questions.question: A product fails to comply with an applicable code or safety rule, but the manufacturer offers a strong warranty and a lower price. The correct disposition is to:

options.A: Keep the product out of the project, because it fails the applicable rule
options.B: Accept the product, since its strong manufacturer warranty offsets the defect
options.C: Accept it as a substitution, carrying the noncompliance at contractor risk
options.D: List the product as an acceptable alternate despite the applicable-rule failure

questions.explanation: A product that fails an applicable code, safety rule, or specified standard must be left out of the project. Neither a strong warranty nor a low price can make up for code noncompliance.

questions.question: In a large gathering space where speech intelligibility suffers from reverberation, the most effective product strategy is to:

options.A: Increase hard reflective surfaces such as polished stone and glass to redistribute the sound
options.B: Minimize hard surfaces and add sound-absorbing acoustical wall panels and acoustical ceilings
options.C: Raise the interior relative humidity, which dampens airborne sound across the gathering space
options.D: Add ultraviolet window tints, which reduce sound transmission through the exterior glazing

questions.explanation: Reverberation in a gathering space is best reduced by cutting back hard surfaces and adding sound-absorbing elements such as acoustical wall panels and high-performance acoustical ceilings.

questions.question: For an indoor swimming pool room, which is the LEAST significant product-evaluation consideration relative to the others?

options.A: Noise control, given the hard wet surfaces that amplify the reverberation
options.B: Resistance to fading, given the limited and indirect daylight in the room
options.C: Humidity control, given the constant moisture load of a natatorium space
options.D: Safety, given the wet floors and the slip hazards around the pool deck

questions.explanation: For a natatorium, humidity control, noise control, and safety are all major concerns, while resistance to fading matters comparatively little — making fading the least significant of the four.

questions.question: For sauna rooms, which interior condition is the most important driver of product and finish selection?

options.A: Sunlight exposure, which would be the dominant degradation factor here
options.B: Humidity control, given the intense moisture and heat that degrade materials
options.C: Lighting level, which would govern the material choices for the interior
options.D: Noise control, which would most affect occupant comfort within the heated space

questions.explanation: Saunas are dominated by intense heat and moisture, so humidity control is the chief driver of product and finish selection, since materials not suited to that environment break down quickly.

questions.question: For a weight room where free weights and equipment are routinely dropped, which building element most warrants careful product selection?

options.A: The ceiling, which must absorb airborne noise from the dropped-weights activity
options.B: The windows, which must resist impact forces through the building structure
options.C: The flooring, which directly absorbs impact from the dropped weights
options.D: The wall paint, which must tolerate the humidity produced by occupants

questions.explanation: The flooring deserves the most careful product selection in a weight room, because the impact of dropped weights and equipment falls most directly on the floor system.

questions.question: In a hospital, infection prevention and control influences finish selection in often-touched areas by favoring:

options.A: Hard surfaces in often-touched areas, so they can be cleaned easily
options.B: Soft, porous textiles that trap contaminants and hold them off the occupants
options.C: Ultraviolet window tints on interior glazing to sterilize touched surfaces
options.D: Maximized corridor carpeting to reduce the footfall noise on touched routes

questions.explanation: Because infection control is critical in hospitals, frequently touched areas favor hard surfaces that can be cleaned often and thoroughly.

questions.question: Where wall finishes and floor coverings risk fading from sunlight through windows, the recommended product strategy is to:

options.A: Specify hard, easily cleaned surfaces throughout the sunlight-exposed locations
options.B: Specify acoustical batts within the exterior walls of the sunlit areas
options.C: Specify single monolithic glazing to admit more daylight to those areas
options.D: Specify ultraviolet window tints where sunlight may fade the finishes

questions.explanation: Where sunlight through windows threatens to fade wall finishes and floor coverings, ultraviolet window tints are the recommended response, addressing the resistance-to-fading concern.

questions.question: An interior product selected without regard to the building's interior climate is most likely to:

options.A: Deteriorate and reduce the useful life of the building, becoming a costly maintenance item
options.B: Automatically exceed the code-required insulation R-values for the building envelope
options.C: Reduce the project's first cost by avoiding the premium charged for climate-rated products
options.D: Improve speech intelligibility and reduce reverberation within the occupied interior space

questions.explanation: A product unsuited to the interior climate tends to deteriorate, shortening the building's useful life and adding maintenance cost. That is why durability has to be judged against the actual interior conditions.

questions.question: When selecting exterior metal surfaces and roofing for a project in a demanding climate, why are high-performance coatings and longer-warranty roof systems favored?

options.A: Because higher-quality coatings reduce maintenance and meet service life
options.B: Because a high-performance coating is always the cheapest first-cost option
options.C: Because low-quality paint and short-warranty roofs satisfy the energy code
options.D: Because premium finishes shift all maintenance liability to the installer

questions.explanation: In a harsh climate, lower-grade paint needs more frequent upkeep than a high-performance coating, and a roof carrying a 20-year warranty should be expected to last that long. Choosing durable, higher-quality products therefore lowers maintenance and helps the assembly reach its intended service life.

questions.question: On the Gulf Coast office building, the contractor's most appropriate initial sequencing consideration is to:

options.A: Construct the brick masonry exterior walls fully before any roofing is set
options.B: Perform some activities out of sequence to finish the project as fast as possible
options.C: Finish the second-floor mechanical and electrical work before any roofing
options.D: Get framing, sheathing, and roof membrane in place to dry-in for interior work

questions.explanation: The key early sequencing move is to dry the building in — get the framing up, sheathing on, and roof membrane installed as the schedule allows — so that interior work is protected from the weather.

questions.question: Which consideration is NOT necessary for product-selection decisions on a Gulf Coast (southeastern) office building?

options.A: Severity of the winter, given the mild winters typical of the Gulf Coast region
options.B: Risk of storm surges, given the building's proximity to coastal water bodies
options.C: Hurricanes, given the building's exposure to the high-velocity coastal wind events
options.D: Amount of sunlight, given the heat gain driving Gulf Coast cooling loads
